entries.question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
alt_phrasings: what is the holy spirit
is the holy spirit a person or a force
entries.answer: The Holy Spirit is presented as a personal being, not merely a force -- one who can be lied to (Acts 5:3-4), who intercedes (Romans 8:26), and whom Jesus calls a Helper who will guide believers into truth (John 14:16-17).

entries.question: If God is good, why does He allow suffering and evil?
alt_phrasings: why does god allow suffering
why is there evil in the world
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't give one single-verse answer; several strands run through it: sin's entry into a good creation brought brokenness (Genesis 3:17-19), God can work even harmful acts toward good ends (Genesis 50:20, of Joseph's brothers selling him into slavery), present suffering works toward a larger purpose for those who love God (Romans 8:28), and suffering is not the final word -- it will one day be ended entirely (Revelation 21:4). This remains one of theology's most discussed questions (the "problem of evil"), and different Christian traditions emphasize different parts of this answer.

entries.question: Did God create Satan, and how did Satan fall?
alt_phrasings: how did satan become evil
who is lucifer
entries.answer:
Scripture: Satan is a created being -- all thrones, powers, rulers and authorities were created through and for Christ (Colossians 1:16). Jesus said, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (Luke 10:18); Revelation 12:7-9 describes war in heaven in which the dragon, "that ancient serpent, called the devil and Satan," and his angels are thrown down; Jude 6 and 2 Peter 2:4 speak of angels who did not keep their positions; and 1 Timothy 3:6 warns against conceit that brings "the same judgment as the devil," pointing to pride.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: God created Satan as a glorious angel -- the "anointed guardian cherub" who was "in Eden, the garden of God" -- who fell through pride and rebelled, drawing a third of the angels with him (Revelation 12:4). Many read Isaiah 14:12-15 ("How you have fallen from heaven, O morning star, son of the dawn!") and Ezekiel 28:12-17 as describing his fall behind the words spoken to the kings of Babylon and Tyre, because the language reaches beyond anything true of a mere man.

Other views: in their immediate context those two passages are addressed to human kings, so the name "Lucifer" (Latin for "morning star" in Isaiah 14:12) and the identification with Satan is an interpretive tradition rather than a direct scriptural statement; the fall itself is directly stated in Luke 10:18 and Revelation 12.

citations.role: read by the Pentecostal/evangelical view as also describing Satan's fall; addressed to the king of Babylon in context
read by the Pentecostal/evangelical view as also describing Satan's fall; addressed to the king of Tyre in context

entries.question: Is God responsible for people's sins?
alt_phrasings: does god tempt people to sin
does god cause sin
entries.answer: No. "God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone. But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed" (James 1:13-14). Sin originates in human desire and choice, not in God, who is perfectly holy.

entries.question: Does God know everything?
alt_phrasings: what is omniscience
is god all knowing
entries.answer: Yes. "God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things" (1 John 3:20); "I declare the end from the beginning, and ancient times from what is still to come" (Isaiah 46:9-10); "His understanding has no limit" (Psalm 147:5).

entries.question: Can our prayers cause God to change His mind?
alt_phrasings: does prayer change god's mind
does prayer actually change anything
entries.answer: Scripture holds two things together rather than resolving them into one simple rule: God's character and ultimate purposes are unchanging ("I the LORD do not change," Malachi 3:6), yet He is shown responding to prayer -- after Moses interceded for Israel, "the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened" (Exodus 32:14), and "The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail" (James 5:16). Christian traditions differ on exactly how to reconcile unchanging sovereignty with real, responsive answers to prayer.

entries.question: Why does it sometimes feel like God is silent?
alt_phrasings: why doesn't god answer me
why does god feel distant
entries.answer: This is a real, recorded experience in scripture itself, not just a modern complaint -- the psalmists cry out "How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?" (Psalm 13:1-2) and "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" (Psalm 22:1-2, the same words Jesus quotes from the cross). Trials are said to test and grow faith (James 1:2-4). Scripture records the experience honestly; it doesn't give one formula for why a particular season of silence occurs.

entries.question: Do Christians and Muslims worship the same God?
alt_phrasings: is allah the same as god
do christianity and islam worship the same god
entries.answer: The New Testament ties knowing God directly to the Son: "No one comes to the Father except through Me" (John 14:6); "Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father" (1 John 2:23); "whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father" (John 5:23). Since Christianity's understanding of God as triune, and of Jesus as God's divine Son who died and rose again, differs fundamentally from Islam's, the historic Christian theological conclusion -- reasoning from these texts -- has generally been that the two faiths, while both tracing roots to Abraham, do not describe the same God in the way each defines Him. The Quran postdates the New Testament by roughly six centuries and is not itself part of the Bible.
entries.note: This is a theological conclusion drawn from these texts, not itself a direct scriptural statement about Islam, which the Bible predates and never mentions.

entries.question: If God knew Adam and Eve would sin, why did He create them?
alt_phrasings: why did god create humans knowing they would sin
why did god allow the fall
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't state this directly as a resolved answer; the traditional theological reasoning is that God valued a genuine, love-based relationship with humanity, which requires real freedom to choose -- and that even the fall would be met with grace, since God "chose us in Him before the foundation of the world" (Ephesians 1:4) and "God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8).

entries.question: Is God male, or a genderless spirit?
alt_phrasings: is god male or female
does god have a gender
entries.answer: "God is spirit" (John 4:24) -- He does not have a physical body or biological sex. Scripture predominantly uses masculine titles for God (Father, King) to express His authority and relationship to His people, not a claim of physical maleness.

entries.question: What does it mean that Jesus is the Son of God?
alt_phrasings: why is jesus called the son of god
entries.answer: The title identifies Jesus's divine nature and unique relationship with the Father, not biological descent -- the Jewish leaders sought to kill Jesus precisely because, by calling God His own Father, "He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God" (John 5:18). Peter's confession, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16), is affirmed by Jesus as revealed by the Father Himself.

entries.question: Did Jesus really rise from the dead?
alt_phrasings: is the resurrection of jesus historical
did jesus physically rise
entries.answer: Yes, per the New Testament's own account: Paul lists specific eyewitnesses to the risen Christ, including more than 500 people at once, most of whom "are still living" at the time he wrote (1 Corinthians 15:3-8); the tomb is found empty and angels announce "He is not here; He has risen, just as He said" (Matthew 28:5-6); the risen Jesus shows His disciples His hands and feet as proof He is not a ghost (Luke 24:39). The bodily resurrection is presented as the foundation the whole Christian faith rests on (1 Corinthians 15:14-17).

entries.question: Is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit the unforgivable sin?
alt_phrasings: what is the unforgivable sin
can the unforgivable sin be forgiven
entries.answer: Jesus states directly: "whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin" (Mark 3:28-30; see also Matthew 12:31-32). This is generally understood as a continuous, willful rejection of the Spirit's testimony about Jesus -- a hardened refusal to repent -- rather than any single sinful act or momentary doubt.

entries.question: Is the Bible completely true and without error?
alt_phrasings: is the bible inerrant
does the bible contain errors
entries.answer: Evangelical Christian doctrine holds that the original manuscripts of scripture are inerrant -- entirely truthful in all they affirm -- based on scripture's own claims about itself: "All Scripture is God-breathed" (2 Timothy 3:16); "no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation" (2 Peter 1:20-21).
entries.note: "Inerrancy" as a formal doctrine is a theological formulation about what these texts imply, not a single verse using that word -- it is widely, though not universally, held across Christian traditions.

entries.question: How was the Bible put together (the Canon)?
alt_phrasings: who decided what books are in the bible
how was the biblical canon formed
entries.answer: The New Testament's books were recognized over the early centuries of the church, generally on the basis of apostolic authorship or direct apostolic endorsement, consistency with already-received doctrine, and widespread acceptance and use across the churches as divinely inspired. Peter already refers to Paul's letters as "Scripture" (2 Peter 3:15-16), and Luke opens his Gospel describing his careful use of eyewitness sources (Luke 1:1-4).
entries.note: The process of canon formation itself is a matter of church history, not something scripture describes about itself in one place.

entries.question: Why is there an Old and a New Testament?
alt_phrasings: what is the difference between the old and new testament
entries.answer: The Old Testament records God's covenant with Israel and points forward to a coming Messiah; the New Testament records the fulfillment of that promise in Jesus and the New Covenant. Jesus states, "I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them" (Matthew 5:17), and Hebrews says of Christ that "the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises" (Hebrews 8:6).

entries.question: What is the Apocrypha, and why is it excluded from Protestant Bibles?
alt_phrasings: what are the apocryphal books
why don't protestants include the apocrypha
entries.answer:
Scripture: the Jews were entrusted with "the very words of God" (Romans 3:2), and Jesus speaks of the Old Testament as "the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms" (Luke 24:44) -- the Hebrew Scriptures, which did not include the Apocrypha. The New Testament quotes the Old Testament hundreds of times but never quotes the Apocryphal books as Scripture.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Bible is the 66 books of the Protestant canon; the Apocrypha, written in the centuries between the Testaments, were never part of the Hebrew Scriptures, contain some material at odds with the rest of the Bible, and are not inspired -- though some are of historical interest.

Other views: the Catholic Church includes several of these books (the deuterocanonical books, such as Tobit, Wisdom and 2 Maccabees) in its Old Testament, and the Orthodox churches include some as well. This app bundles the 66-book canon plus, clearly labeled as non-canonical, 1 Enoch.

entries.question: Which Bible translation is the best?
alt_phrasings: what is the most accurate bible translation
which translation should i use
entries.answer: There is no single "best" translation -- word-for-word (formal equivalence) translations like the ESV, NASB, or KJV are generally favored for close study, while thought-for-thought (dynamic equivalence) translations like the NIV are often praised for readability. Scripture itself values both accuracy and clarity of understanding (Nehemiah 8:8 describes the Levites reading the Law "clearly" and giving its meaning; 1 Corinthians 14:9 values intelligible speech).
entries.note: This is a practical recommendation, not a scriptural statement -- scripture doesn't rank translations, which didn't exist in their modern form when it was written.

entries.question: How should a beginner start reading the Bible?
alt_phrasings: where should i start reading the bible
best book of the bible for beginners
entries.answer: A common recommendation is to begin in the New Testament with the Gospel of John, written explicitly "that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God" (John 20:31), then Romans for its systematic explanation of the gospel, then the Old Testament book of Genesis for the origins of the story John and Romans presuppose.
entries.note: This is practical reading guidance, not a scriptural command about reading order.

entries.question: Are Christians still required to follow Old Testament laws?
alt_phrasings: do christians have to keep the mosaic law
which old testament laws still apply
entries.answer: The common Christian position holds that believers are under the New Covenant, not the Mosaic law as a whole (Romans 6:14): the law's civil regulations (for governing ancient Israel specifically) and ceremonial regulations (sacrifices, dietary rules, purity codes) are widely held to have been fulfilled in Christ (Galatians 3:24-25; Matthew 5:17), while its moral commands -- summarized in the Ten Commandments -- are generally held to reflect God's unchanging character and to remain binding. Christian traditions vary in exactly how they draw these distinctions.

entries.question: Should Christians keep the Saturday Sabbath?
alt_phrasings: do christians have to worship on saturday
is sunday worship biblical
entries.answer: Most Christian traditions hold that the Sabbath was a sign specific to the Mosaic covenant with Israel, and that the early church came to gather on Sunday ("the Lord's Day") to commemorate Christ's resurrection (Acts 20:7 describes believers gathering "on the first day of the week"). Paul explicitly warns against judging one another over which day is observed (Romans 14:5; Colossians 2:16-17). A minority of Christian traditions (including Seventh-day Adventists) continue to hold a Saturday Sabbath as binding.

entries.question: Is the Bible historically accurate?
alt_phrasings: is the bible historically reliable
does archaeology confirm the bible
entries.answer: Many biblical narratives name specific, real historical rulers and places that are independently attested (Luke, for instance, carefully dates events against named Roman and regional rulers: Luke 3:1-2). Proponents point to a substantial and growing body of archaeological and historical findings as corroborating many people, places, and events named across the biblical narrative.
entries.note: Historical/archaeological corroboration is an ongoing scholarly matter, evaluated case by case -- this is a general claim about the Bible's historical character, not a single verse's statement.

entries.question: What does it mean that the Bible is "living and active"?
alt_phrasings: what does living and active mean in hebrews
why is the bible called living and active
entries.answer: "the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit... it judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart" (Hebrews 4:12). This describes scripture as more than historical record -- something the Holy Spirit actively uses to expose motives and transform readers across every generation.

entries.question: Can a Christian lose their salvation?
alt_phrasings: can you lose your salvation
is salvation permanent or conditional
can a born again christian go back to sin and still be saved
entries.answer:
Scripture: "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Corinthians 5:17). Salvation is a free gift, bought by the death and blood of Christ (Ephesians 2:8-9; 1 Peter 1:18-19) -- but that same grace teaches us "to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives" (Titus 2:11-12), and it is never a license to keep on sinning (Romans 6:1-2, 15; Jude 4). Scripture warns that going back to the old life puts a person at risk: "If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains" (Hebrews 10:26); Jesus says the branch that does not remain in Him is thrown away and withers (John 15:1-6); "Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven" (Matthew 7:21); "holiness, without which no one will see the Lord" (Hebrews 12:14); and to the lukewarm church in Laodicea Jesus says, "you are neither cold nor hot. How I wish you were one or the other! So because you are lukewarm — neither hot nor cold — I am about to vomit you out of My mouth!" (Revelation 3:15-16). Peter describes those who escaped the world's corruption and are again entangled in it as a dog returning to its vomit (2 Peter 2:20-22). Scripture is equally clear that believers who stumble and repent are forgiven -- "if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father — Jesus Christ, the Righteous One" (1 John 2:1; 1:9) -- and that nothing outside can take a believer from Christ's hand (John 10:27-29; Romans 8:38-39).

Pentecostal understanding: salvation is a gift given freely by God and paid for by the death and blood of Christ, but it is not a "get out of jail free card." The person who is born again becomes a new creation and strives, in the power of the Holy Spirit, to live a new life; a heart that has really been changed does not go on living as it did before. A person who is reborn and then returns to the old ways of sin and keeps living as before -- lukewarm, or cold -- is in danger of losing what he was given. The difference is between falling short in weakness and repenting, which the blood forgives, and willfully turning back, which scripture warns against. The believer who abides in Christ has real assurance (1 John 5:13; Philippians 1:6).

Other views: many Baptist and Reformed churches teach eternal security -- that a truly born-again person can never finally fall away, and that those who do were never truly saved (1 John 2:19).

citations.role: stated: grace teaches us to live differently
stated: not a license to sin
stated: forgiveness for the believer who stumbles
stated (Christ's keeping of those who follow Him)

entries.question: Is Jesus the only way to heaven?
alt_phrasings: is jesus the only way to god
can you get to heaven without jesus
entries.answer: Yes, per Jesus's own explicit claim: "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me" (John 14:6). Peter preaches the same exclusivity: "Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved" (Acts 4:12).

entries.question: What is sin?
alt_phrasings: how does the bible define sin
entries.answer: Scripture defines it in more than one way: "sin is lawlessness" -- transgressing God's standard (1 John 3:4); "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" -- missing God's perfect standard (Romans 3:23); and "anyone, then, who knows the good he ought to do and doesn't do it, sins" -- sins of omission as well as commission (James 4:17).

entries.question: What is the difference between justification and sanctification?
alt_phrasings: what does justification mean
what does sanctification mean
entries.answer: Standard Protestant theological terms: justification is a one-time legal declaration -- God declaring a believer righteous on the basis of Christ ("having been justified by faith, we have peace with God," Romans 5:1); sanctification is the ongoing, lifelong process of being made holy and Christlike (Philippians 1:6 -- "He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion").

citations.role: supporting: sanctification as an ongoing work

entries.note: "Justification" and "sanctification" as a formal paired distinction are theological vocabulary describing what these texts teach, not the texts' own terminology.

entries.question: Is water baptism required for salvation?
alt_phrasings: do you have to be baptized to be saved
is baptism necessary for salvation
what is baptism
what is water baptism
why should i be baptized
entries.answer:
Scripture: "it is by grace you have been saved through faith... not by works" (Ephesians 2:8-9), and the thief on the cross was promised paradise with no opportunity to be baptized (Luke 23:42-43). At the same time baptism is plainly commanded: Jesus tells His disciples to baptize (Matthew 28:19), Peter says "repent and be baptized" (Acts 2:38), and Cornelius's household was baptized after they received the Holy Spirit (Acts 10:44-48). Jesus says "whoever believes and is baptized will be saved," but the condemnation He names falls on the one who does not believe (Mark 16:16).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: water baptism by immersion is a command of Christ, an act of obedience and the public testimony of the new birth -- it follows repentance and faith and belongs to every believer -- but it is faith in the shed blood of Jesus, not the water, that saves.

Other views: the Catholic and Orthodox churches, the Church of Christ, and Oneness Pentecostals teach that baptism is itself necessary for, or a means of, salvation.

citations.role: stated: baptized after receiving the Spirit

entries.question: What does predestination mean?
alt_phrasings: what is election in the bible
does god choose who gets saved
entries.answer:
Scripture: God "chose us in Him before the foundation of the world" and "predestined us for adoption" (Ephesians 1:4-5); "those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son" (Romans 8:29-30); "No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him" (John 6:44). Scripture equally says God "wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:4), is "not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance" (2 Peter 3:9), and invites "the one who is thirsty" to come and take the water of life freely (Revelation 22:17).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: election is in Christ and according to God's foreknowledge (Romans 8:29; 1 Peter 1:2); the gospel is genuinely offered to "whosoever will," and each person must answer the Father's drawing in faith -- God's sovereign purpose and human responsibility are both taught in scripture. This is the common Pentecostal view.

Other views: Calvinist/Reformed churches teach unconditional election -- that God chose particular individuals for salvation apart from any foreseen faith.

citations.role: stated: God wants all to be saved

entries.question: How can I forgive myself for past sins?
alt_phrasings: how do i stop feeling guilty about my past
how do i let go of guilt
entries.answer: Scripture's answer centers on accepting what God has already done, rather than a separate act of "self-forgiveness": "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9); "there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1); "as far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us" (Psalm 103:12).

entries.question: Can a deathbed conversion really save someone?
alt_phrasings: can you be saved right before you die
is it too late to be saved at the end of life
entries.answer: Yes -- scripture's own clearest example is the criminal crucified beside Jesus, who simply asked to be remembered, with no opportunity for any further works: Jesus answered, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in paradise" (Luke 23:42-43). Salvation isn't based on time served or accumulated works (illustrated also in the parable of the workers hired at the eleventh hour, Matthew 20:1-16), but on grace received through faith, whenever it is genuinely placed in Christ.

entries.question: Why do Christians still sin if they are a "new creation"?
alt_phrasings: why do christians still struggle with sin
if i'm saved why do i still sin
entries.answer:
Scripture: "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Corinthians 5:17). Paul is honest about the struggle: "the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh" (Galatians 5:17); "I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do" (Romans 7:15-25). John says believers who claim to be without sin deceive themselves, yet promises forgiveness and cleansing to those who confess (1 John 1:8-9) and an Advocate if anyone does sin (1 John 2:1) -- while also saying that the one born of God does not go on sinning (1 John 3:9). Paul answers, "Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase? Certainly not!" (Romans 6:1-2), promises that sin shall not be master over believers (Romans 6:14), and says, "walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh" (Galatians 5:16).

Pentecostal understanding: the new birth makes a real change -- a new heart and new desires -- and the believer, filled with the Holy Spirit, strives every day to put off the old life and live the new, with power over sin through the Spirit (Romans 8:1-4, 13). Falling short in weakness and repenting is different from returning to the old ways and living as before: the first is forgiven by the blood (1 John 1:7-9); the second is a warning sign (see the question on losing salvation).

Other views: some traditions teach that the believer remains a sinner in this life until glorified and is not expected to be free from sin before then; holiness churches teach that entire sanctification is possible now.

entries.question: What happens to a Christian immediately when they die?
alt_phrasings: what happens when a believer dies
where does a christian go right after death
entries.answer: The majority Christian view holds that a believer's soul immediately enters the conscious presence of the Lord, awaiting the final bodily resurrection: "would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord" (2 Corinthians 5:8); "to depart and be with Christ... is far better" (Philippians 1:23); Jesus tells the criminal beside Him, "today you will be with Me in paradise" (Luke 23:43). A minority of Christian traditions have historically held a "soul sleep" view (unconscious rest until the resurrection) instead.

entries.question: Is Hell a real place of literal fire and torment?
alt_phrasings: is hell eternal
does hell really exist
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus speaks of "the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels" and of "eternal punishment" for the unrighteous, set against "eternal life" for the righteous (Matthew 25:41, 46); of a place "where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’" (Mark 9:43-48); and, in the account of the rich man and Lazarus, of conscious torment in Hades and a great chasm that cannot be crossed (Luke 16:19-31). Revelation says "the smoke of their torment rises forever and ever," that the devil, the beast and the false prophet are tormented day and night forever, and that anyone not found in the Book of Life is thrown into the lake of fire (Revelation 14:11; 20:10, 15).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: hell is real -- a place of eternal, conscious punishment and separation from God for those who reject Christ. That is why the Church preaches the gospel with urgency: God is "not wanting anyone to perish" (2 Peter 3:9), and Jesus bore the penalty in the shed blood of the cross so that no one need go there.

Other views: some evangelical scholars hold annihilationism (the unsaved are finally destroyed rather than tormented forever), and a few hold universalism (all are eventually saved); both depart from the reading above.

entries.question: Will pets or animals go to heaven?
alt_phrasings: do animals have souls
will i see my pet again in heaven
entries.answer: Scripture never directly states whether individual pets or animals have eternal souls or an afterlife. What it does describe is a restored creation full of animal life -- "The wolf will live with the lamb... the lion will eat straw like the ox" (Isaiah 11:6-9), and "the wolf and the lamb will feed together" in the New Earth's peace (Isaiah 65:25). This app won't claim scripture answers the pets question directly when it doesn't.

citations.role: stated: animal life in restored creation
stated: animal life in restored creation

entries.question: Can someone who commits suicide go to heaven?
alt_phrasings: does suicide send you to hell
is suicide unforgivable
entries.answer:
Scripture: the Bible records several people who took their own lives (Saul, 1 Samuel 31:4; Ahithophel, 2 Samuel 17:23; Judas, Matthew 27:5) and never says that suicide is the unforgivable sin -- the one sin Jesus calls unforgivable is persistent blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (Matthew 12:31-32). Scripture says God alone sees the heart (1 Samuel 16:7; Psalm 139:1-4), that He is "compassionate and gracious" and that "He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust" (Psalm 103:8, 14), and that each of us will give account to Him (Romans 14:10-12). Life is God's gift and belongs to Him (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

Pentecostal understanding: no one can say for certain where a particular person stands before God -- that judgment belongs to Him alone -- and scripture gives grieving families grounds to entrust their loved one to a merciful God, while teaching that our standing before Him rests on a living relationship with Christ, not on a single moment. The Church's calling is to point the hurting to Christ and to sit with the grieving in prayer and love.

Other views: some traditions have treated suicide as a grave sin that puts a person's salvation in doubt, while others stress that a believer's standing rests on Christ's finished work; pastors and traditions counsel grieving families differently.

If you are struggling with thoughts of ending your life, please tell someone right now -- a pastor, a doctor, or a crisis line where you live. You are not alone, and help is available.

citations.role: stated: the one sin called unforgivable
stated: each will give account to God

entries.question: Will we recognize our loved ones in heaven?
alt_phrasings: will i know my family in heaven
do we keep our identity in heaven
entries.answer: Scripture suggests continued, even fuller, recognition and relationship: "Now we see but a dim reflection... then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known" (1 Corinthians 13:12); at the Transfiguration, Peter, James, and John recognize Moses and Elijah despite having never met them (Matthew 17:3); David expects to be reunited with his deceased infant son (2 Samuel 12:23).

entries.question: Is Purgatory mentioned in the Bible?
alt_phrasings: what is purgatory
does the bible teach purgatory
entries.answer:
Scripture: it is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment (Hebrews 9:27); the believer who departs is "at home with the Lord" (2 Corinthians 5:8; Philippians 1:23; Luke 23:43); Jesus taught that after death a great chasm is fixed between the righteous and the wicked that no one can cross (Luke 16:26); and "the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7), for "by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified" (Hebrews 10:14). Purgatory is not named or described anywhere in the 66 books of the Bible.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: there is no purgatory. The blood of Jesus fully pays for and cleanses every sin of the one who trusts Him, so nothing remains to be purged after death; the believer goes at once to be with the Lord, and the unbeliever to judgment.

Other views: the Catholic Church teaches purgatory as a state of purification after death, grounding it in church tradition, in 2 Maccabees 12:43-46 (a book outside the Protestant canon), and in its reading of 1 Corinthians 3:15.

citations.role: stated: the blood cleanses from all sin

entries.question: Do humans become angels when they die?
alt_phrasings: do people turn into angels after death
are angels dead humans
entries.answer: No. Humans and angels are described as entirely distinct kinds of created beings -- Hebrews calls angels "ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation" (Hebrews 1:14), implying angels serve humans, not that humans become them. Believers are said to one day judge angels (1 Corinthians 6:3), and humans were made "a little lower than the angels" (Psalm 8:4-5), a distinct rank, not a stage humans graduate into.

entries.question: What will our resurrected bodies be like?
alt_phrasings: what kind of body do christians get in heaven
will we have physical bodies after death
entries.answer: Physical, immortal, and glorious: "sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body" -- imperishable, free from decay (1 Corinthians 15:42-44); Christ "will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body" (Philippians 3:21); "when Christ appears, we will be like Him" (1 John 3:2).

entries.question: What is the New Jerusalem?
alt_phrasings: what is the heavenly city
what does revelation say about the new jerusalem
entries.answer: A magnificent city John sees descending from God to the New Earth in his vision -- "I saw the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God" -- described as God's eternal dwelling place among His redeemed people, where "there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain" (Revelation 21:1-4, with its structure described in detail in Revelation 21:10-27).

entries.question: Will there be marriage or families in heaven?
alt_phrasings: are you married to your spouse in heaven
does marriage continue after death
entries.answer: Jesus states directly that earthly marriage does not continue in the resurrection: "In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven" (Matthew 22:30; also Mark 12:25) -- said in response to a question testing Him about a woman widowed multiple times.

entries.question: What are the primary signs of the End Times?
alt_phrasings: what are the signs of jesus's return
how will we know the end is near
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus lists wars and rumors of wars, famines and earthquakes, persecution, false christs and false prophets, growing lawlessness, love growing cold, and the gospel preached to the whole world as a witness before the end comes (Matthew 24:4-14). Paul warns of perilous, self-loving, godless times in the last days (2 Timothy 3:1-5), and Jesus says, when these things begin to happen, "stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near" (Luke 21:28). Peter says the outpouring of the Holy Spirit "on all people" -- sons and daughters prophesying -- marks the last days (Acts 2:17, quoting Joel 2:28).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: these signs point to the nearness of the Lord's return. The Pentecostal movement sees the worldwide outpouring of the Spirit as part of the fulfillment of Joel 2 in the last days, and holds that believers are to watch and be ready for the Rapture, which is imminent and needs no sign to precede it.

Other views: Christians differ on how literally, and on what timetable, to apply these signs; some read much of Matthew 24 as fulfilled in AD 70 or as describing the whole church age.

citations.role: stated: the outpouring of the Spirit in the last days

entries.question: What is the Rapture?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about the rapture
when will the rapture happen
entries.answer:
Scripture: "the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command... and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise. After that, we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will always be with the Lord" (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). "We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed — in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet" (1 Corinthians 15:51-52). Jesus promised to come again and receive His own to Himself (John 14:3), and Paul calls it "the blessed hope" (Titus 2:13).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Rapture is the imminent, any-moment catching up of the Church -- the dead in Christ raised and living believers changed -- to meet the Lord in the air, before the Tribulation. Believers are promised rescue from the coming wrath (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 5:9) and to be kept "from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world" (Revelation 3:10), so the Church watches and waits for Him rather than expecting to endure that period.

Other views: some Christians place the Rapture at the middle or the end of the Tribulation, and many (including Catholic, Orthodox and Reformed churches) read these passages as describing a single, final return of Christ with no separate Rapture.
entries.note: The word "Rapture" is not in English translations; it comes from the Latin rapiemur ("we shall be caught up") in 1 Thessalonians 4:17. The passages state the catching up itself; its timing before the Tribulation is the Pentecostal/evangelical reading of them, presented here as that reading.

entries.question: Who is the Antichrist?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about the antichrist
who is the man of lawlessness
entries.answer:
Scripture: Paul describes "the man of lawlessness," who exalts himself, takes his seat in God's temple, and proclaims himself to be God (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4, 8-9); Daniel sees a boastful "little horn" who persecutes the saints (Daniel 7:8, 24-25); Revelation describes the beast, given authority to blaspheme and to make war on the saints (Revelation 13:1-8). John says both that "antichrist is coming" and that "many antichrists have come" -- anyone who denies the Father and the Son (1 John 2:18, 22).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: there is a real, future individual -- the Antichrist, the man of lawlessness -- who rises to world power, is revealed after the Church is taken up in the Rapture (2 Thessalonians 2:6-8, reading "the one now restraining" as the Holy Spirit working through the Church), makes a covenant with Israel and breaks it (Daniel 9:27), and is destroyed by Christ at His return (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The many antichrists of John's day are forerunners of the spirit he embodies.

Other views: some traditions read "antichrist" mainly as a continuing spirit or system of false teaching (as 1 John 4:3 also says), or identify him with a historical institution rather than a single future person.

citations.role: stated (the restrainer, read by the Pentecostal/evangelical view as the Spirit through the Church)
stated (many antichrists already, and one to come)

entries.question: What is the Mark of the Beast?
alt_phrasings: what is 666
what does the mark of the beast mean
entries.answer:
Scripture: the beast forces everyone -- small and great, rich and poor, free and slave -- to receive a mark on the right hand or the forehead, so that no one can buy or sell without it; its number is 666, "the number of a man" (Revelation 13:16-18). Those who worship the beast and receive its mark drink the wine of God's wrath (Revelation 14:9-11), while those who refuse it, though martyred, reign with Christ (Revelation 20:4).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: this is a literal mark, imposed during the Tribulation after the Rapture, that seals a person's allegiance to the Antichrist and his system; taking it is a final, irreversible rejection of God. The believer's assurance is that the Church is kept from that hour (Revelation 3:10) and is sealed instead by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 1:13).

Other views: some interpreters read the mark and the number symbolically -- total allegiance to a power opposed to God -- rather than as a literal future mark.

citations.role: supporting: believers are sealed by the Spirit

entries.question: What is the Tribulation?
alt_phrasings: what is the great tribulation
how long is the tribulation
entries.answer:
Scripture: Daniel's prophecy of seventy weeks ends with one final "week" -- seven years -- in which the coming ruler makes a covenant and breaks it in the middle of the week (Daniel 9:24-27). Jeremiah calls it "the time of Jacob’s distress" (Jeremiah 30:7). Jesus speaks of "great tribulation, unmatched from the beginning of the world until now" (Matthew 24:21), and Revelation 6-19 describes the seals, trumpets and bowls of judgment poured out on the earth.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Tribulation is a literal seven-year period of unprecedented judgment on the earth, following the Rapture of the Church and ending with the visible return of Christ. The second half -- the "great tribulation" of 42 months (Revelation 11:2-3; 12:6, 14; 13:5) -- is led by the Antichrist; many Jews and Gentiles are saved during it, and the Church is not present (Revelation 3:10; 1 Thessalonians 5:9).

Other views: preterists hold that most of these prophecies were fulfilled in the first century (the fall of Jerusalem, AD 70); amillennialists read the tribulation as the whole church age; mid- and post-tribulation Christians place the Church within it.

entries.question: What is the Millennial Kingdom?
alt_phrasings: what is the 1000 year reign of christ
is the millennium literal or symbolic
entries.answer:
Scripture: Revelation 20:1-6 describes Satan bound for a thousand years and the saints who "came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years." The prophets foretell the Messiah reigning on David's throne with peace and justice (Isaiah 9:6-7; 11:1-10) and the LORD becoming King over all the earth (Zechariah 14:9); the angel told Mary her Son would reign over the house of Jacob forever (Luke 1:32-33).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: this is premillennial -- Christ returns visibly after the Tribulation and reigns on earth for a literal thousand years from Jerusalem, with Satan bound and the resurrected saints reigning with Him (Revelation 20:4-6; 2 Timothy 2:12), fulfilling God's promises to Israel and to creation. After it come Satan's final rebellion and the Great White Throne judgment (Revelation 20:7-15).

Other views: amillennialists (most of historic Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran and Reformed theology) read the thousand years as symbolic of Christ's present reign through the church; postmillennialists expect the gospel to bring a golden age before Christ returns.

entries.question: Can anyone predict the exact date of Christ's return?
alt_phrasings: do we know when jesus is coming back
can you calculate the date of the second coming
entries.answer: No -- and this is one point virtually all Christian traditions agree on. Jesus states plainly: "no one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father" (Matthew 24:36; Mark 13:32). When His own disciples asked directly, Jesus told them: "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority" (Acts 1:7). Anyone claiming to have calculated a specific date is going beyond what scripture itself allows.

entries.question: What is the Battle of Armageddon?
alt_phrasings: what is armageddon in the bible
where is armageddon
entries.answer:
Scripture: spirits of demons gather the kings of the whole world "for the battle on the great day of God the Almighty," at the place called Armageddon (Revelation 16:14-16). Then heaven opens and the Faithful and True, Christ, rides out with the armies of heaven; the beast and the false prophet are seized and thrown into the lake of fire, and the rest are destroyed by the word of His mouth (Revelation 19:11-21). Zechariah 14:1-4 pictures the LORD's feet standing on the Mount of Olives as He fights for Jerusalem.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: Armageddon is the literal climax of the Tribulation, in which the nations gather under the Antichrist against Israel and are defeated by Christ's visible, bodily return with His saints -- leading directly into the Millennial reign.

Other views: many interpreters read the battle scene symbolically, as the final victory of Christ over evil, rather than as a single literal military engagement.

entries.question: What is the Great White Throne Judgment?
alt_phrasings: what is the final judgment
what happens at the last judgment
what is the judgment seat of christ
what is the bema seat judgment
entries.answer:
Scripture: John sees "a great white throne" and the dead, small and great, standing before it; books are opened, including the Book of Life, and the dead are judged according to what they had done; anyone whose name is not found in the Book of Life is thrown into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:11-15). Jesus speaks of "the resurrection of life" and "the resurrection of judgment" (John 5:28-29). Believers, by contrast, will appear before the judgment seat of Christ -- not for condemnation but to be rewarded for their works (2 Corinthians 5:10; Romans 14:10-12; 1 Corinthians 3:11-15) -- for "there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: these are two different judgments -- the Judgment Seat of Christ for believers, after the Rapture, where the redeemed (washed in His blood) receive rewards; and the Great White Throne at the end of the Millennium, where the unsaved dead are judged and sentenced to the lake of fire.

Other views: many traditions hold a single general judgment at Christ's return rather than separate judgments a thousand years apart.

citations.role: stated: the judgment seat of Christ

entries.question: Will Christians go through the Tribulation?
alt_phrasings: will the church experience the tribulation
is the rapture before or after the tribulation
entries.answer:
Scripture: "God has not appointed us to suffer wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Thessalonians 5:9); Jesus is "our deliverer from the coming wrath" (1 Thessalonians 1:10); and to the faithful church at Philadelphia He promises, "I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world" (Revelation 3:10).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Church is taken up in the Rapture before the Tribulation begins (the pre-tribulation Rapture), so believers do not go through the wrath of that period; people who come to faith during it are a separate company (Revelation 7:9-14). Believers still face ordinary tribulation in this world (John 16:33).

Other views: mid- and post-tribulation Christians read Matthew 24:29-31 ("immediately after the distress of those days") as placing the gathering of believers after the Tribulation, and non-futurist traditions do not expect a separate seven-year period at all.

citations.role: supporting: those saved during the Tribulation

entries.question: What does the Bible say about homosexuality?
alt_phrasings: is being gay a sin according to the bible
what does the bible say about same sex relationships
entries.answer:
Scripture: God made humanity male and female and joined a man and his wife in marriage (Genesis 1:27; 2:24; Matthew 19:4-6). The Law forbids a man lying with a man as with a woman (Leviticus 18:22; 20:13). Paul describes same-sex relations as contrary to nature and God's design (Romans 1:26-27) and lists the sexually immoral, including homosexual offenders, among those who will not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9-10; 1 Timothy 1:10) -- and immediately adds the hope of the gospel: "And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God" (1 Corinthians 6:11).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: homosexual practice, like every sexual act outside the marriage of one man and one woman, is sin; but the blood of Christ cleanses every sinner, the new birth changes lives, and those who struggle are to be met with truth, love and grace, not contempt.

Other views: some churches and scholars today read these texts as addressing exploitative practices rather than committed same-sex relationships and affirm such relationships; that is not how the historic Christian church, or the reading given here, understands them.

entries.question: Is sex before marriage a sin?
alt_phrasings: is premarital sex a sin
does the bible allow sex before marriage
entries.answer: Scripture repeatedly commands believers to avoid "sexual immorality" (a broad term, Greek porneia, covering sex outside marriage) and reserves sexual intimacy for the marriage relationship: "Flee from sexual immorality" (1 Corinthians 6:18); "Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled" (Hebrews 13:4); "each of you must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor" (1 Thessalonians 4:3-4).

entries.question: When is divorce permitted for a Christian?
alt_phrasings: does the bible allow divorce
is divorce a sin
what did jesus say about divorce
jesus teaching on divorce
what does the bible say about divorce
what does the bible say about divorce and remarriage
entries.answer:
Scripture: God's design is a lifelong union -- "what God has joined together, let man not separate" (Matthew 19:6) -- and "I hate divorce," says the LORD (Malachi 2:16). Jesus allows one exception: "whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman, commits adultery" (Matthew 19:9). Paul adds that if an unbelieving spouse leaves, "The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases" (1 Corinthians 7:15), and that a believer who does separate should remain unmarried or be reconciled (1 Corinthians 7:10-11).

Pentecostal understanding: marriage is meant to be permanent, and the church's first call is to repentance, forgiveness and restoration. Most Pentecostal churches recognize the two grounds scripture gives -- sexual unfaithfulness and desertion by an unbelieving spouse -- and counsel careful pastoral care in each case.

Other views: the Catholic Church teaches that a valid sacramental marriage cannot be dissolved and deals with failed marriages through annulment; some Christians allow divorce on wider grounds, and others allow none.

entries.question: Is masturbation a sin?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say masturbation is wrong
entries.answer: The act itself is never named or directly addressed anywhere in scripture. The traditional Christian reasoning applying to it draws on adjacent principles instead -- Jesus's teaching that lustful intent is itself a form of adultery "in his heart" (Matthew 5:28), calls to self-control (1 Thessalonians 4:4-5), and warnings against "evil desires" broadly (Colossians 3:5) -- but this is an application of those principles, not a direct scriptural statement about the act itself, and Christians who agree on those underlying principles still reach differing pastoral conclusions.

entries.question: Are Christians allowed to get tattoos?
alt_phrasings: is it a sin to get a tattoo
does the bible forbid tattoos
entries.answer:
Scripture: Leviticus 19:28 forbids tattoo marks along with cutting the body for the dead -- given to Israel against the background of pagan mourning and cultic practice. The New Testament gives no rule about tattoos, but teaches that the believer's body is the temple of the Holy Spirit and is to honor God (1 Corinthians 6:19-20), that everything is to be done for God's glory (1 Corinthians 10:31), and that whatever is not from faith is sin (Romans 14:23).

Pentecostal understanding: many Pentecostal and holiness churches counsel against tattoos, on the ground of the body as the Spirit's temple and a holy, set-apart life (Leviticus 19:28; 1 Corinthians 6:19-20); others treat the matter as one of individual conscience before the Lord, judged by motive and content.

Other views: most other traditions regard tattoos as a matter of Christian liberty, reading Leviticus 19:28 as a pagan-mourning prohibition specific to Israel.

entries.question: Is drinking alcohol a sin?
alt_phrasings: does the bible forbid alcohol
is it a sin to drink
entries.answer:
Scripture: it condemns drunkenness clearly -- "Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to reckless indiscretion. Instead, be filled with the Spirit" (Ephesians 5:18); "Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler" (Proverbs 20:1); drunkards will not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:10); and Proverbs 23:29-35 vividly warns of its woes. It also records wine in ordinary use (John 2:1-11; 1 Timothy 5:23) and warns against causing a weaker brother to stumble (Romans 14:21). Scripture does not, in so many words, forbid every drink.

Pentecostal understanding: the Pentecostal and holiness tradition teaches total abstinence -- because Ephesians 5:18 sets being drunk with wine against being filled with the Spirit, because the believer's body is the Spirit's temple (1 Corinthians 6:19-20), for the sake of a clear witness, and out of love for those who could be led into addiction (Romans 14:21). Many Pentecostal churches ask this of their members and ministers.

Other views: many Christian traditions (Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican, Lutheran, Reformed) permit moderate drinking, reading scripture as condemning drunkenness rather than alcohol itself.

entries.question: Is gambling a sin?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say gambling is wrong
is it a sin to play the lottery
entries.answer: Gambling itself is never named in scripture. The traditional Christian caution against it is drawn from adjacent warnings -- against the love of money ("the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil," 1 Timothy 6:10), against trying to get rich quickly (Proverbs 13:11), and against serving money as a master (Matthew 6:24) -- an application of these principles rather than a direct command.

entries.question: Are Christians required to tithe 10% of their income?
alt_phrasings: do christians have to tithe
is tithing required in the new testament
entries.answer:
Scripture: Abraham gave a tenth to Melchizedek long before the Law (Genesis 14:20; Hebrews 7:1-8), Jacob vowed a tenth (Genesis 28:22), and the Law required it (Leviticus 27:30). Malachi says withholding the tithe and offerings is robbing God and promises blessing to those who "bring the full tithe into the storehouse" (Malachi 3:8-10). Jesus, speaking of the Pharisees' tithing, says they should have practiced justice, mercy and faithfulness "without neglecting the former" -- that is, the tithe (Matthew 23:23). The New Testament also urges giving that is cheerful, generous and proportionate (2 Corinthians 9:6-7; 1 Corinthians 16:2), and it does not state a separate percentage for the church.

Pentecostal understanding: most Pentecostal churches teach the tithe -- the first tenth of one's income -- as the biblical baseline of giving, with freewill offerings beyond it, given cheerfully as an act of worship and trust that God will provide.

Other views: some Christians hold that the tithe belonged to the Mosaic law and that New Covenant giving is free-will without a fixed percentage.

citations.role: stated: Abraham's tithe, before the Law

entries.question: Is viewing pornography a sin?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say pornography is wrong
entries.answer: Jesus states the underlying principle directly: "anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Matthew 5:28); Job describes making a personal covenant not to look with lust (Job 31:1); John warns against "the desires of the eyes" (1 John 2:16). Pornography is not named by that word (a modern term), but these texts speak directly to its core content -- deliberately cultivated lustful looking.

entries.question: Is using foul language a sin?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say cursing is a sin
is swearing wrong biblically
entries.answer: "Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up" (Ephesians 4:29); "you must put aside all such things as these... filthy language from your lips" (Colossians 3:8).

citations.role: supporting: what comes out of the mouth can defile

entries.question: Does the Bible support evolution?
alt_phrasings: is evolution compatible with the bible
does genesis rule out evolution
entries.answer:
Scripture: God created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1), each plant and creature "according to its kind" (Genesis 1:11-12, 21, 24-25), and made man in His own image, male and female (Genesis 1:26-27), forming Adam from the dust of the ground and breathing into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). All things were created through Christ (Colossians 1:16), and Exodus 20:11 grounds the week in six days of creation.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: God directly and purposefully created the universe, the kinds of living things, and Adam and Eve as real, historical persons made in His image (special creation); humanity did not descend from lower animals.

Other views: theistic evolutionists (evolutionary creationists) hold that God used evolution as His means of creating and read Genesis 1-2 as theological rather than scientific description; this is a real position among Christians who all affirm God as Creator.

entries.question: How old is the Earth according to the Bible?
alt_phrasings: how old is the earth
does the bible say how old the earth is
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't state the earth's age directly. Young-earth creationists calculate roughly 6,000-10,000 years by totaling the genealogies from Genesis 1 forward. Old-earth creationists allow for a much older earth, reading Genesis's creation "days" less literally and pointing to texts like "in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes" (Psalm 90:4) and "with the Lord a day is like a thousand years" (2 Peter 3:8) as evidence scripture itself doesn't demand strict calendar-day reckoning of God's timescale. Both positions are held by serious, scripture-affirming Christians.

entries.question: Were the days in Genesis literal 24-hour days?
alt_phrasings: are the days of creation literal
what does yom mean in genesis
entries.answer: Literal-day creationists point to the Hebrew word "yom" (day) being paired with "evening, and there was morning" (Genesis 1:5) and to Exodus 20:11, which grounds the seven-day work week in a literal six-day creation, as indicating ordinary 24-hour days. Day-Age creationists read "yom" as capable of denoting a longer, indefinite period elsewhere in scripture and understand the creation days as long geological epochs. Both readings remain live positions among conservative biblical scholars.

entries.question: Does the Bible mention dinosaurs?
alt_phrasings: are dinosaurs in the bible
what are behemoth and leviathan
entries.answer: The word "dinosaur" (coined in 1841) doesn't appear, since it postdates the Bible by millennia. Job describes two enormous creatures, "Behemoth" (Job 40:15-24) and "Leviathan" (Job 41:1-34), in vivid, larger-than-life terms. Some young-earth creationists read these descriptions as depicting dinosaur-like animals coexisting with humans. Many other scholars -- including conservative ones -- read Behemoth as a hippopotamus or elephant and Leviathan as a crocodile or as poetic imagery for a sea monster/chaos figure (compare Psalm 74:14; Isaiah 27:1), consistent with the book of Job's heavily poetic style throughout. This app presents both readings rather than asserting the dinosaur identification as settled.

entries.question: Where did Cain get his wife?
alt_phrasings: who did cain marry
how did cain have a wife if he was the only son
entries.answer: Scripture states Adam and Eve had "other sons and daughters" beyond Cain, Abel, and Seth (Genesis 5:4), so Cain's wife (Genesis 4:17) was almost certainly a sister or other close relative -- something the text doesn't spell out explicitly but implies, since no other population of humans is described as existing at that point. The additional apologetic argument that such close-relative marriage "did not carry genetic risk before mutations accumulated" is a traditional/scientific argument some apologists make to address the ethical question, not itself a claim scripture makes.

citations.role: stated: other unnamed sons and daughters

entries.note: The genetic-risk reasoning is a modern apologetic argument, not a scriptural claim -- separated out here so it isn't presented with the same certainty as what the text actually states.

entries.question: Was Noah's Flood global or local?
alt_phrasings: was the flood worldwide or regional
did the flood cover the whole earth
entries.answer: Genesis describes the flood covering "all the high hills under the whole heaven" and destroying "every living thing... on the face of the earth" outside the ark (Genesis 7:19-23), language most naturally read, and most traditionally held, as a global catastrophe. A minority of conservative scholars read this same language as describing a regional flood covering the whole of the world as known/inhabited by Noah at the time, similar to how other biblical texts use "all the earth" in a regionally-bounded sense elsewhere. 2 Peter 3:6 refers back to "the world of that time" being destroyed by the flood.

entries.question: Does the Bible oppose scientific exploration?
alt_phrasings: is the bible against science
does christianity oppose science
entries.answer: No. Scripture presents an orderly universe reflecting God's glory and invites study of it: "The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of His hands" (Psalm 19:1); "Great are the works of the LORD; they are pondered by all who delight in them" (Psalm 111:2); "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out" (Proverbs 25:2).

entries.question: Who were the Nephilim?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about the nephilim
were the nephilim giants
entries.answer: Genesis 6:4 describes the Nephilim as present "when the sons of God went to the daughters of men and had children by them" -- described as "heroes of old, men of renown." The identity of "the sons of God" is genuinely disputed: one major reading (drawing on the term's use elsewhere for angelic/heavenly beings, e.g. Job 1:6) holds they were fallen angels who intermarried with human women; another reading holds "sons of God" refers to the godly line of Seth intermarrying with Cain's line. Numbers 13:33 later uses "Nephilim" again, of large/intimidating inhabitants the spies encountered in Canaan.

citations.role: stated: a later use of the term

entries.question: What was the Tower of Babel?
alt_phrasings: what happened at babel
why did god confuse the languages
entries.answer: A unified human project to build a great city and tower "that reaches to the heavens," explicitly to "make a name for ourselves" rather than fill the earth as God had commanded. God responds by confusing their language so they could no longer understand each other, scattering them across the earth (Genesis 11:1-9).

entries.question: Does the Bible condemn interracial marriage?
alt_phrasings: is interracial marriage a sin
does the bible forbid marrying outside your race
entries.answer: No. Scripture's marriage boundaries are spiritual, not racial -- forbidding marriage between believers and unbelievers (2 Corinthians 6:14), not marriage across ethnicity. All humanity is described as descending from one common origin (Acts 17:26, "From one man He made all the nations"), and in Christ ethnic distinctions carry no spiritual hierarchy: "There is neither Jew nor Greek... for you are all one in Christ Jesus" (Galatians 3:28). Moses himself married a Cushite (Ethiopian) woman (Numbers 12:1).

citations.role: stated: the real boundary is spiritual
example: Moses married a Cushite woman

entries.question: Are guardian angels biblical?
alt_phrasings: does everyone have a guardian angel
do angels protect us
entries.answer: Angels are shown actively guarding and serving believers -- "He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways" (Psalm 91:11); Jesus refers to children having angels who "always see the face of My Father" (Matthew 18:10); angels are called "ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation" (Hebrews 1:14). Scripture doesn't explicitly confirm the popular idea of one specific angel permanently assigned to each individual person.

entries.question: Can a true Christian be demon-possessed?
alt_phrasings: can a believer be possessed by a demon
can christians be controlled by demons
entries.answer:
Scripture: the believer's body is the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19); "greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world" (1 John 4:4); "the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him" (1 John 5:18); the Lord "will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one" (2 Thessalonians 3:3). Yet believers are also told the devil prowls seeking someone to devour and must be resisted (1 Peter 5:8-9; Ephesians 6:11-12), not to give him a foothold (Ephesians 4:27), and Jesus gave His followers authority to cast out demons in His name (Mark 16:17; Luke 10:17-19).

Pentecostal understanding: a blood-bought, Spirit-filled believer belongs to Christ and cannot be possessed by a demon, but can be oppressed, tempted and attacked from outside, and can give the enemy a foothold through sin; the answer is repentance, resistance, and the believer's authority in Jesus' name -- with deliverance ministry for those in bondage.

Other views: some deliverance ministries teach that a believer can have a demon dwelling in some part of his life; some cessationist churches do not practice deliverance at all.

entries.question: What is spiritual warfare?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about spiritual warfare
entries.answer: "our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world’s darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms" (Ephesians 6:11-12) -- an invisible conflict believers engage through prayer, scriptural truth, and what Paul calls the "full armor of God" (Ephesians 6:11), resisting a real adversary who "prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour" (1 Peter 5:8), using "divine power to demolish strongholds" rather than worldly weapons (2 Corinthians 10:3-5).

entries.question: Is speaking in tongues required for all Christians?
alt_phrasings: do all christians speak in tongues
is tongues a sign of salvation
what is the baptism in the holy spirit
is speaking in tongues the evidence of the holy spirit
entries.answer:
Scripture: on the Day of Pentecost, all who were filled with the Holy Spirit "began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit enabled them" (Acts 2:4); the same happened when the Spirit fell on Cornelius's household (Acts 10:44-46) and on the disciples at Ephesus (Acts 19:6). The promise of the Spirit is "to you and your children and to all who are far off" (Acts 2:38-39). Yet Paul lists tongues among the gifts given "as He determines" and asks, "Do all speak in tongues?" (1 Corinthians 12:11, 30), while wishing that all did (1 Corinthians 14:5) and thanking God that he speaks in tongues more than all of them (1 Corinthians 14:18).

Pentecostal understanding: two different things are being described. The baptism in the Holy Spirit is a distinct experience promised to every believer (Luke 11:13; Acts 1:5, 8), and its initial evidence is speaking in other tongues, as in Acts 2, 10 and 19. The ministry gift of tongues with interpretation for the assembly (1 Corinthians 12:10; 14:27-28) is a different thing, given to some and not to all -- which is why Paul's question "Do all speak?" concerns the public gift. Every believer may be Spirit-baptized and pray in tongues; not every believer has the gift of tongues for public ministry.

Other views: non-Pentecostal evangelicals hold that tongues is a gift some receive and not the evidence of Spirit baptism; cessationists hold that tongues ceased with the apostolic age.

citations.role: stated: the promise is for all

entries.note: The distinction between the baptism in the Holy Spirit (with tongues as initial evidence) and the ministry gift of tongues is the Pentecostal reading of these texts; the passages themselves state what happened and what Paul says about the gift.

entries.question: Does God still perform miracles and physical healings today?
alt_phrasings: does god still heal people today
are miracles still happening
entries.answer:
Scripture: "I am the LORD, who heals you" (Exodus 15:26); "by His stripes we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5); "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever" (Hebrews 13:8). Jesus said signs would accompany believers -- "they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well" (Mark 16:17-18); "gifts of healing" are among the gifts of the Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:9); and James tells the sick to call the elders to pray and anoint with oil, for "the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up" (James 5:14-15). Scripture is also honest that not every case ends in healing: Paul's thorn in the flesh (2 Corinthians 12:7-9), Timothy's frequent illnesses (1 Timothy 5:23), and Trophimus left sick (2 Timothy 4:20).

Pentecostal understanding: divine healing and miracles are part of Christ's finished work and continue today -- through prayer, the laying on of hands, anointing with oil, and the gifts of the Spirit. The same Jesus who healed in the Gospels heals now, and the Church is to expect and pray for the sick.

Other views: cessationists teach that the miraculous sign gifts ceased with the apostles, though most still affirm that God can and does heal in answer to prayer.

citations.role: stated: not every prayer ends in healing

entries.question: Should Christians avoid horoscopes, tarot cards, and psychics?
alt_phrasings: is astrology a sin
can christians use tarot cards
entries.answer: Yes. Scripture forbids divination, sorcery, interpreting omens, witchcraft, and mediumship in strong terms: "Let no one be found among you who... practices divination or conjury, interprets omens, practices sorcery, casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist... For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD" (Deuteronomy 18:10-12); such practices are listed among the "works of the flesh" that exclude one from God's kingdom (Galatians 5:19-21).

entries.question: How can I discern God's will for my life?
alt_phrasings: how do i know god's will for me
how do you find god's will
entries.answer: Scripture points to several practices rather than one formula: "Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind" so you can "test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God" (Romans 12:2); regular engagement with scripture ("Your word is a lamp for my feet," Psalm 119:105); trusting God rather than your own understanding (Proverbs 3:5-6); and seeking counsel ("plans succeed with many advisers," Proverbs 11:14).

entries.question: What does it mean to "lay out a fleece" to know God's will?
alt_phrasings: what is gideon's fleece
asking god for a sign like gideon
entries.answer: The phrase comes from Gideon, who asked God for two specific, physical signs involving a wool fleece before he would trust he'd correctly understood his call to lead Israel (Judges 6:36-40). God accommodated Gideon's request, but this is generally read as an example of God's patience with weak faith, not a model practice to imitate -- the New Testament calls believers instead to "walk by faith, not by sight" (2 Corinthians 5:7), and Jesus rebukes a general demand for miraculous signs as evidence of unbelief (Matthew 12:39).

entries.question: Are there different ranks of angels and demons?
alt_phrasings: are there different types of angels
what are archangels
entries.answer: Yes. Scripture names multiple tiers among heavenly and spiritual beings -- "rulers... authorities... powers of this world’s darkness... spiritual forces of evil" (Ephesians 6:12), "thrones or powers or rulers or authorities" created through Christ (Colossians 1:16), the archangel Michael (Jude 1:9), and angels who "did not keep their positions of authority" (Jude 6).

entries.question: What is spiritual discernment?
alt_phrasings: how do you discern good and evil spiritually
what is the gift of discernment
entries.answer: The Spirit-given ability to distinguish truth from error and recognize what pleases God -- "solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil" (Hebrews 5:14); "test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world" (1 John 4:1); Paul prays believers' "love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight, so that you may be able to test and prove what is best" (Philippians 1:9-10).

entries.question: Can women serve as pastors or elders?
alt_phrasings: can women be pastors
can women be church leaders
can women be elders
entries.answer:
Scripture: God has used women in leadership and ministry again and again. Miriam, a prophetess, led Israel in worship (Exodus 15:20; Micah 6:4). Deborah, a prophetess and judge, led Israel (Judges 4:4-5). Huldah the prophetess was consulted by the king about the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22:14-20). Anna the prophetess spoke about the child Jesus to all who were waiting for redemption (Luke 2:36-38). Mary Magdalene was the first sent to tell others the Lord had risen (John 20:17-18). Philip's four daughters prophesied (Acts 21:9). Phoebe was a servant (deacon) of the church at Cenchreae (Romans 16:1). Priscilla, with her husband Aquila, explained the way of God to Apollos, and Paul calls them his fellow workers (Acts 18:26; Romans 16:3). Euodia and Syntyche labored beside Paul in the gospel (Philippians 4:2-3). The Spirit is poured out on "sons and daughters" who prophesy (Joel 2:28-29; Acts 2:17-18), and in Christ "There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female" (Galatians 3:28). Scripture also teaches that the husband is head of the household (Ephesians 5:23; 1 Corinthians 11:3) and praises the strong, capable wife whose wisdom builds up her home (Proverbs 31:10-31; 14:1). The passages that seem to restrict women's teaching or authority are 1 Timothy 2:12, 1 Timothy 3:2 and 1 Corinthians 14:34-35.

Pentecostal understanding: yes -- women can be leaders, elders and pastors. God has used women in leadership and ministry throughout scripture, often for very specific purposes; the gifts and calling of the Spirit are given to daughters as well as sons; and the Pentecostal movement was born with women preaching, prophesying, planting churches and serving as pastors and missionaries. The man may be the head of the household, but headship in the home and calling in the church are different questions, and a strong godly wife is often what makes a household and a ministry succeed. The restricting passages are read as addressing particular first-century situations of disorder and false teaching, not as a permanent ban on women in ministry.

Other views: many Baptist and Presbyterian churches, and the Catholic and Orthodox churches, read 1 Timothy 2:12 and 3:2 as limiting the office of pastor, elder or priest to qualified men, and some Pentecostal bodies also reserve the pastor or elder office for men.
