entries.question: What are the main differences between Protestants and Catholics?
alt_phrasings: how is catholicism different from protestantism
protestant vs catholic beliefs
entries.answer:
Scripture: salvation is by grace through faith, not by works (Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 3:28); all Scripture is God-breathed and equips the man of God for every good work (2 Timothy 3:16-17); there is "one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 2:5), and believers have direct access through their great High Priest to "the throne of grace" (Hebrews 4:14-16); all believers are "a royal priesthood" (1 Peter 2:9); and Paul pronounces a curse on any "gospel" other than the one preached (Galatians 1:6-9).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: Scripture alone is the final authority (sola scriptura); a sinner is justified by grace alone through faith alone in the blood of Christ (sola fide); every believer is born again by the Spirit and has direct access to God through Christ, without an earthly priesthood; and the church has two ordinances, baptism and the Lord's Supper.

Other views: Catholic teaching holds that Scripture and sacred Tradition together, interpreted by the Church's teaching office (the Magisterium), are authoritative; that salvation involves grace working through faith, the sacraments and good works; that the Pope is Christ's earthly head of the church; and that Mary and the saints intercede for believers. Protestants and Catholics differ on each of these points.

entries.question: Are Jehovah's Witnesses and Mormons Christian?
alt_phrasings: is the church of jesus christ of latter day saints christian
are jehovah's witnesses trinitarian
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus is the eternal Word who "was God" and became flesh (John 1:1, 14); in Him "all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form" (Colossians 2:9); He shares equality with God (Philippians 2:5-11); and "Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father" (1 John 2:22-23). Paul warns that even if an angel from heaven preaches a gospel other than the one already preached, "let him be under a curse!" (Galatians 1:8-9), and John says not to welcome one who does not abide in the teaching of Christ (2 John 9-11). There is one God (Isaiah 44:6; 1 Timothy 2:5).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: by the standard of scripture's teaching on Christ's eternal deity, the Trinity, and salvation by grace through faith in His blood, Jehovah's Witnesses (who teach that Jesus is a created being, identified with the archangel Michael, and reject the Trinity) and Mormons (who teach a different doctrine of God, including a plurality of gods, and of Jesus) do not hold biblical Christianity, even though both use the name of Christ. Their people are to be met with love and a clear gospel witness.

Other views: both groups regard themselves as Christian, and some other traditions are more reluctant to draw that line.
entries.note: Scripture does not name either modern group; the second paragraph applies scripture's teaching on Christ and the gospel to their stated doctrine.

entries.question: Why are there so many different Christian denominations?
alt_phrasings: why are there so many churches
why is christianity so divided
entries.answer: Most denominational differences concern secondary matters -- church governance structure, baptism mode/timing, end-times views, worship style -- rather than the core essentials most denominations still affirm together (Christ's deity, His death and resurrection, salvation by grace). Paul both calls for unity ("that all of you agree... and that there be no divisions among you," 1 Corinthians 1:10; "one body and one Spirit... one Lord, one faith, one baptism," Ephesians 4:3-6) and instructs believers not to quarrel over disputable matters (Romans 14:1-4).

entries.question: Is church attendance mandatory for a Christian?
alt_phrasings: do christians have to go to church
is going to church required for salvation
entries.answer: Attending church doesn't itself save anyone -- salvation is by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8-9) -- but scripture directly commands believers not to stop meeting together: "Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another" (Hebrews 10:24-25). The earliest church is described devoting itself to "the apostles' teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer" together (Acts 2:42), and believers are described as interdependent members of one body (1 Corinthians 12:27).

entries.question: What is transubstantiation?
alt_phrasings: does the bread and wine become jesus's body
what is the catholic view of communion
entries.answer:
Scripture: at the Last Supper Jesus took bread and said, "This is My body," and the cup, "the new covenant in My blood," adding "do this in remembrance of Me" (Luke 22:19-20); Paul says that as often as believers eat and drink, "you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes" (1 Corinthians 11:23-26). Jesus also said, "The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life" (John 6:63), and Hebrews stresses that Christ offered one sacrifice for sins "once for all" (Hebrews 10:10-14).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Lord's Supper is an ordinance of remembrance and proclamation -- the bread and cup symbolize Christ's body broken and blood shed for us -- taken in faith with self-examination (1 Corinthians 11:28), not a repetition of the sacrifice.

Other views: the Catholic Church teaches transubstantiation -- that the bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ while keeping their appearance -- and that the Mass makes that sacrifice present; Lutherans teach the real presence "in, with and under" the elements without a change of substance.

citations.role: stated: one sacrifice, once for all

entries.question: What is church discipline?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about church discipline
how should a church handle unrepentant sin
entries.answer: A formal process Jesus outlines for confronting an unrepentant believer: go to them privately first, then with one or two witnesses, then before the church, with removal from fellowship as a last resort if they still refuse to repent (Matthew 18:15-17). Paul instructs the Corinthian church to remove an unrepentant member from fellowship for the purpose of ultimately restoring him (1 Corinthians 5:1-5), and Galatians instructs restoring a fallen believer "gently," watching one's own heart in the process (Galatians 6:1).

entries.question: What is the biblical definition of the church?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible mean by the church
is the church a building
entries.answer: Not a building, but people: "the church, which is His body" (Colossians 1:18; Ephesians 1:22-23) -- the global body of all true believers in Jesus Christ, described as "in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body" (1 Corinthians 12:13), manifesting locally in specific congregations that gather.

entries.question: What are the biblical ordinances for the local church?
alt_phrasings: what are the sacraments of the church
what did jesus command the church to practice
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus commands His disciples to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19), and gave the Lord's Supper with the command to keep doing it in remembrance of Him (Luke 22:19; 1 Corinthians 11:23-26). He also washed His disciples' feet and told them to do as He had done (John 13:14-15).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: two ordinances instituted by Christ -- water baptism by immersion, and the Lord's Supper -- observed as acts of obedience and testimony rather than as channels of saving grace. Some Pentecostal and holiness churches also observe foot washing as an ordinance (John 13:14-15).

Other views: the Catholic and Orthodox churches teach seven sacraments (baptism, confirmation, the Eucharist, penance, anointing of the sick, holy orders and matrimony) as means of grace.

entries.question: What is the role of a church deacon?
alt_phrasings: what does a deacon do
what are the qualifications for a deacon
entries.answer: The role originates with seven men chosen to manage the daily distribution of food to widows, freeing the apostles to focus on prayer and preaching (Acts 6:1-6) -- deacons are described as qualified servants who manage practical, administrative, and charitable needs within the church, with specific character qualifications listed in 1 Timothy 3:8-13.

entries.question: Can a Christian see a secular therapist or psychiatrist?
alt_phrasings: is it okay for christians to go to therapy
can christians take medication for mental health
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't address modern psychiatry or therapy directly, so this is an application of broader principles rather than a direct command: seeking wise counsel is commended generally ("plans succeed with many advisers," Proverbs 11:14), while believers are cautioned to "test all things. Hold fast to what is good" (1 Thessalonians 5:21) and not to be taken captive by thinking that contradicts Christ (Colossians 2:8). Most Christian traditions today affirm that medical/psychological treatment can address real biological and psychological factors alongside -- not instead of -- spiritual care, with all advice filtered through scripture.
entries.note: The source document cited a nonexistent reference ("Protestants 11:14") here -- corrected to Proverbs 11:14, the most plausible intended verse, when this entry was checked against scripture.

entries.question: How should a Christian handle anxiety and depression?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about anxiety
how do christians deal with depression
entries.answer: "Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God" (Philippians 4:6-7); "Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you" (1 Peter 5:7); the psalmist models honest lament in the midst of depression: "Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me?" (Psalm 42:11). Most Christian traditions today also affirm pursuing medical treatment for depression/anxiety with a biological component, alongside prayer and Christian community, rather than treating these practices as opposed to each other.

entries.question: How can I discover my spiritual gifts?
alt_phrasings: how do i find my spiritual gift
what are the spiritual gifts
entries.answer: Scripture names various specific gifts (Romans 12:6-8; 1 Corinthians 12:4-7) given "to each one... for the common good," but doesn't prescribe a step-by-step discovery process. The commonly taught practical approach is active service in a local church, noticing where that service bears fruit, and receiving confirmation from church leadership and community (1 Peter 4:10, "use whatever gift you have received to serve others").

entries.question: What does it mean to take care of your body as a temple?
alt_phrasings: what does body as a temple mean
why does the bible say the body is a temple
entries.answer: "Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you... You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20) -- treating one's physical body, which belongs to God and houses His Spirit, with respect, avoiding what scripture elsewhere names as harmful (sexual immorality, substance abuse) and doing all things, including eating and drinking, for God's glory (1 Corinthians 10:31; Romans 12:1).

entries.question: How do I balance supporting family with helping the poor?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say to help family first or the poor
who comes first family or charity
entries.answer: Scripture places providing for one's own family as a serious, primary obligation -- "If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever" (1 Timothy 5:8) -- while also commanding generosity toward the vulnerable: "Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress" (James 1:27); "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD" (Proverbs 19:17); giving is to flow "out of... abundance," for a fair balance, not at the expense of one's own basic needs (2 Corinthians 8:13-14).

entries.question: What does the blood of Jesus do?
alt_phrasings: is the blood of jesus enough to save me
what does it mean to be washed in the blood
what does it mean that jesus's blood bought us
why is the blood of jesus important
what does the bible say about the blood of jesus
what does blood bought mean
entries.answer:
Scripture: the blood of Jesus bought us. The church of God was "purchased with His own blood" (Acts 20:28); "you were bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:20); we were redeemed "not with perishable things such as silver or gold... but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot" (1 Peter 1:18-19); and the redeemed sing to the Lamb, "by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation" (Revelation 5:9). It washes away our sin: "the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7); in Him "we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses" (Ephesians 1:7); and those before the throne "have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb" (Revelation 7:14). It is God's appointed payment for sin: "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness" (Hebrews 9:22; Leviticus 17:11), foreshadowed when the blood on the doorposts made the LORD pass over Israel's houses (Exodus 12:13). Through it we are justified and saved from wrath (Romans 5:9), have peace with God through "the blood of His cross" (Colossians 1:20), and have "confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus" (Hebrews 10:19). Believers overcome the accuser "by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony" (Revelation 12:11).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the blood-bought life. The death and shed blood of Jesus are the once-for-all price that redeems the sinner from sin, death and the power of the enemy. Yes, the blood is enough to save -- there is nothing to add to it, and the gift is received freely by repentance and faith (Romans 3:25). Because we were bought with a price, we belong to Him (1 Corinthians 6:19-20) and are called to live as His purified people, "zealous for good deeds" (Titus 2:14). The blood is never a license to keep on sinning: to go on deliberately sinning is to trample the Son of God underfoot and treat "the blood of the covenant" as unclean (Hebrews 10:26-29). Believers plead the blood in prayer for cleansing, protection and victory over the enemy (Revelation 12:11).

Other views: Christian traditions explain the atonement in different ways (as substitution, as ransom, as victory over evil), and Catholic and Orthodox teaching links the blood of Christ closely with the Eucharist; all affirm that the cross is the basis of forgiveness.

entries.question: Who were the parents of John the Baptist?
alt_phrasings: who were john the baptist's parents
who was john the baptist's father
who was john the baptist's mother
who is the father of john the baptist
who is the mother of john the baptist
john the baptist parents
who were zechariah and elizabeth
who was elizabeth's husband
who was zacharias
entries.answer: John the Baptist's father was Zechariah, a priest of the division of Abijah, and his mother was Elizabeth, a descendant of Aaron (Luke 1:5). Both were righteous before God, but they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren and they were well along in years (Luke 1:6-7). An angel told Zechariah, “Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John” (Luke 1:13). When the child was born Elizabeth said, “He shall be called John,” and Zechariah wrote, “His name is John” (Luke 1:60-63). Luke later calls him “John son of Zechariah” (Luke 3:2).
entries.note: The King James Version spells the names Zacharias and Elisabeth.

entries.question: Was John the Baptist a cousin of Jesus?
alt_phrasings: were john the baptist and jesus related
was john the baptist jesus's cousin
how were john the baptist and jesus related
who was elizabeth to mary
was elizabeth mary's cousin
was elizabeth related to mary
how old was john the baptist compared to jesus
was john older than jesus
entries.answer: Scripture says that Elizabeth, John's mother, was Mary's relative. The angel told Mary, “Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age” (Luke 1:36); the King James Version calls her Mary's “cousin”. John was about six months older than Jesus: Elizabeth was in her sixth month when the angel came to Mary (Luke 1:26, 36), and Mary then stayed with Elizabeth about three months (Luke 1:39-45, 56). So John and Jesus were relatives through their mothers. The Bible does not say exactly how Elizabeth and Mary were related; “cousin” is the traditional way of putting it.
entries.note: The Greek word in Luke 1:36 means a relative or kinswoman; the Bible does not give the exact relationship.

entries.question: How does Satan try to influence or attack a believer?
alt_phrasings: how does satan work in a believer's life
ways the enemy attacks christians
how does the devil tempt christians
how does satan influence you
7 ways satan attacks
how to resist the devil
what are the devil's schemes
how does the enemy attack me
spiritual warfare how satan works
entries.answer: Scripture does not give a numbered list, but it shows the enemy at work in these ways, each with the answer to it. Deception: he is a liar and the father of lies (John 8:44) and disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). Taking the word away: the devil comes and takes the word from hearts so that people may not believe (Luke 8:12); the same parable says worries, riches and pleasures of this life also choke the word (Luke 8:14), though it does not name the devil as the cause of those. Temptation: the tempter came to Jesus in the wilderness, who answered every time with “It is written” (Matthew 4:1-11). Accusation: Satan stood at Joshua's right hand “to accuse him” (Zechariah 3:1), and he is called the accuser of the brothers (Revelation 12:10), but “there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:1). Fear and anxiety: “Cast all your anxiety on Him,” and “Resist him, standing firm in your faith” (1 Peter 5:7-9). Anger and division: “do not give the devil a foothold” (Ephesians 4:26-27). Friendship with the world: “Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you” (James 4:4-8). And the assurance: “greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world” (1 John 4:4); “we are not unaware of his schemes” (2 Corinthians 2:11).

entries.note: Grouping into seven ways is a teaching summary, not a list in Scripture.

entries.question: What does the Bible say about Christ in you?
alt_phrasings: christ in you the hope of glory
life in christ
what does it mean that christ lives in me
what do i have in christ
who am i in christ
complete in christ
fruit of the spirit and gifts of the spirit
the holy spirit in the believer
what does the bible say about the indwelling spirit
entries.answer: What Scripture says: the mystery is “Christ in you, the hope of glory” (Colossians 1:27), and Paul can say, “Christ lives in me” (Galatians 2:20). The believer's body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19). In Christ you are “made complete” (Colossians 2:10), and Christ has become our wisdom from God, righteousness, holiness and redemption (1 Corinthians 1:30). Through God's promises we become “partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4). “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength” (Philippians 4:13). All authority has been given to Jesus (Matthew 28:18), God is able to do immeasurably more than we ask or imagine by His power at work within us (Ephesians 3:20), and “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you” (Acts 1:8). The Spirit produces fruit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control (Galatians 5:22-23), and gives gifts to each one as He determines (1 Corinthians 12:4-11): the message of wisdom, the message of knowledge, faith, gifts of healing, the working of miracles, prophecy, distinguishing between spirits, speaking in various tongues and the interpretation of tongues.

citations.role: more than we ask or imagine

views.label: The Pentecostal reading
views.text: the Spirit who lives in every believer from new birth also fills believers with power for witness (Acts 1:8; 2:4), and the gifts of 1 Corinthians 12 are for the church today.

views.label: Other views
views.text: many other traditions hold that all believers receive the Spirit at conversion and that some gifts, such as tongues and healing, belonged to the apostolic age.

entries.question: Who are the heroes of faith in Hebrews 11?
alt_phrasings: heroes of the faith
hall of faith
faith heroes of the bible
who is listed in hebrews 11
by faith people in the bible
list of people of faith in the bible
entries.answer: Hebrews 11 opens with “Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see” and then tells what faith did in the lives of: Abel, who offered a better sacrifice (verse 4); Enoch, who was taken so that he did not see death (5); Noah, who built an ark (7); Abraham, who obeyed and went out not knowing where (8-10) and offered up Isaac (17-19); Sarah, who counted the one who had promised as faithful (11); Isaac (20), Jacob (21) and Joseph (22), who each looked ahead in blessing or instruction; Moses, whose parents hid him and who chose to suffer with God's people (23-28); the people who crossed the Red Sea and the walls of Jericho that fell (29-30); and Rahab, who welcomed the spies (31). Verse 32 adds Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets, and verses 33-38 describe others without naming them. The chapter ends by saying that all of these were commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised, because God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect (verses 39-40).
entries.note: Names follow the verses; some lists of heroes of faith leave out Sarah, Barak, Samson and Jephthah, who are named here.

entries.answer:
Genesis gives each father's age when the next son in the line was born and how long he lived, so the whole line from Adam to Abraham can be added up (years counted from creation, not BC). The longest life was Methuselah, 969 years (Genesis 5:27). Enoch, at 365 years, did not die: “God took him away” (Genesis 5:23-24). Adding the figures:
Adam: born year 0, lived 930, died year 930
Seth: born year 130, lived 912, died year 1042
Enosh (Enos): born year 235, lived 905, died year 1140
Kenan (Cainan): born year 325, lived 910, died year 1235
Mahalalel (Mahalaleel): born year 395, lived 895, died year 1290
Jared: born year 460, lived 962, died year 1422
Enoch: born year 622, lived 365, died year 987
Methuselah: born year 687, lived 969, died year 1656
Lamech: born year 874, lived 777, died year 1651
Noah: born year 1056, lived 950, died year 2006

Arphaxad: born year 1658, lived 438, died year 2096
Shelah (Salah): born year 1693, lived 433, died year 2126
Eber: born year 1723, lived 464, died year 2187
Peleg: born year 1757, lived 239, died year 1996

Nahor: born year 1849, lived 148, died year 1997

The flood came in Noah's 600th year (Genesis 7:6), which is year 1656 on this count, the year Methuselah died.

entries.note: Added up from the figures in the Masoretic-based text the BSB and KJV follow. The Septuagint and the Samaritan Pentateuch give different numbers. “Became the father of” can mean an ancestor, so a count like this is the text's own total, not a proven date. Abram's birth year depends on a choice: counted from Terah's death at 205 and Abram's leaving Haran at 75 it is year 2008 (as here); if Abram was born when Terah was 70 (Genesis 11:26) it is year 1948.

entries.question: How can I pray without ceasing?
alt_phrasings: pray without ceasing meaning
how to pray always
how to pray throughout the day
what does pray in the spirit mean
how do i pray at all times
how to pray daily
how to make prayer a habit
entries.answer: What Scripture says: “Pray without ceasing” (1 Thessalonians 5:17). Jesus told a parable about “their need to pray at all times and not lose heart” (Luke 18:1). Paul says, “Pray in the Spirit at all times, with every kind of prayer and petition” (Ephesians 6:18). It can be woven through the day: “whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God” (Colossians 3:17); turn worries into prayer, “in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God” (Philippians 4:6-7), and “Cast all your anxiety on Him” (1 Peter 5:7); thanksgiving over food is part of it (1 Timothy 4:4-5); there is prayer at the start of the day (Psalm 5:3; Mark 1:35); and the Word shapes the praying, as the one who meditates on the Law of the LORD day and night (Joshua 1:8; Psalm 1:2). It is not waiting for a feeling: “the Spirit helps us in our weakness” when we do not know how to pray (Romans 8:26).

citations.role: pray in the Spirit at all times
everything in the Lord's name with thanks

views.label: The Pentecostal reading
views.text: praying in the Spirit includes praying in tongues, “I will pray with my spirit” (1 Corinthians 14:14-15; Jude 20), a way to stay in prayer through the day.

views.label: Other views
views.text: many traditions understand “in the Spirit” as prayer led and empowered by the Holy Spirit without tongues.

entries.question: What are the lands of the Bible called today?
alt_phrasings: bible lands then and now
biblical lands and their modern names
modern names of bible lands
what is canaan today
where is nineveh today
where was ur
what country is babylon
what is persia today
where was edom
where was moab
what is the modern name of aram
where is sheba today
where was midian
entries.answer: The lands of the Bible keep their names in Scripture but sit in different countries today. Canaan (Genesis 12:5): now Israel and the Palestinian territories, with parts of Lebanon, western Jordan and south-west Syria; Persia (Ezra 1:1): now Iran; Babylonia (Babylon, Chaldea, Shinar) (Daniel 1:1): now southern and central Iraq; Aram (2 Kings 5:1): now Syria (Aram-naharaim reached into northern Mesopotamia); Phoenicia (Tyre and Sidon) (Acts 11:19): now the coast of Lebanon, reaching into northern Israel and southern Syria; Asia, Galatia, Pontus and the other provinces of Asia Minor (1 Peter 1:1): now Turkey (Anatolia); Cush (Genesis 10:6): now Nubia: the south of Egypt and northern Sudan. Many Bibles render it “Ethiopia”, but that is not modern Ethiopia (not certain); Put (Genesis 10:6): now usually Libya (the Libyan coast); some scholars suggest the Red Sea coast further south (not certain); Sheba (1 Kings 10:1): now south-west Arabia (Yemen) is the usual view; some place it in Ethiopia (not certain); Edom (Seir) (Genesis 36:1): now southern Jordan and the Negev in Israel; Moab (Genesis 19:37): now the plateau east of the Dead Sea, in Jordan; Ammon (Genesis 19:38): now the area of Amman, Jordan; Philistia (Psalms 87:4): now the southern coastal plain of Israel and the Gaza Strip; Gilead (Numbers 32:1): now the hill country east of the Jordan, in northern Jordan; Bashan (Numbers 21:33): now the Golan Heights and the Hauran plateau, in south-west Syria and northern Jordan; Midian (Exodus 2:15): now north-west Arabia (Saudi Arabia) and southern Jordan; the borders are uncertain (not certain); Nineveh (Jonah 1:2): now beside Mosul in northern Iraq (the mounds of Kuyunjik and Nebi Yunus); Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:31): now traditionally Tell el-Muqayyar near Nasiriyah, southern Iraq (some scholars propose a site further north) (traditional identification); Haran (Genesis 11:31): now Harran in south-eastern Turkey, near the Syrian border; Lud (Genesis 10:22): now not certain: often linked to Lydia in western Turkey (not certain). Borders in the Bible moved with the nations, so these are regions rather than exact lines; where the identification is uncertain it says so.

citations.role: Asia, Galatia, Pontus and the other provinces of Asia Minor

entries.note: Which modern places match which ancient lands is a matter of scholarship; the uncertain ones are marked.

entries.question: How old was Methuselah when he died?

methuselah age

entries.answer: Methuselah lived 969 years, the longest life recorded in Scripture (Genesis 5:27).

entries.question: How old was Adam when he died?
alt_phrasings: how long did adam live
how old was adam
adam age at death
how many years did adam live
entries.answer: Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died (Genesis 5:5).

how old was noah
noah age at death
how many years did noah live
entries.answer: Noah lived a total of 950 years: he was 600 years old when the flood came (Genesis 7:6), and after the flood he lived another 350 years (Genesis 9:28-29).

entries.question: How many books are in the New Testament?

number of books in the new testament
how many books in the nt
entries.answer: The New Testament has 27 books: the four Gospels, Acts, 21 letters and Revelation.
entries.note: The grouping of the books is the one the churches have used since the fourth century; the 27 are the New Testament of the canon bundled in this app.

entries.question: How many books are in the Old Testament?
alt_phrasings: how many books does the old testament have
number of books in the old testament
how many books in the ot
entries.answer: The Old Testament has 39 books in the Protestant order used in this app (the Jewish Bible holds the same writings counted as 24, and some churches add more books).
entries.note: How the writings are counted and which books are included differs between Jewish, Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox Bibles.

entries.question: How many days was Jesus tempted in the wilderness?
alt_phrasings: how long was jesus in the wilderness
how long did jesus fast

entries.answer: Forty days and forty nights: Jesus fasted that long in the wilderness, and then the tempter came to Him (Matthew 4:1-2); Mark and Luke also say He was tempted for forty days (Mark 1:13; Luke 4:2).

entries.question: How tall was Goliath?
alt_phrasings: how big was goliath
how tall was the giant goliath
goliath height
what size was goliath
entries.answer: The Bible says Goliath was “six cubits and a span in height” (1 Samuel 17:4). A cubit is about 18 inches (45 cm), which makes about 9 feet 9 inches (nearly 3 metres).
entries.note: Some ancient manuscripts (the Septuagint and a Dead Sea scroll of Samuel) read “four cubits and a span”, about 6 feet 9 inches; the length of a cubit also varied.

entries.question: Who betrayed Jesus?

who handed jesus over
who sold jesus for thirty pieces of silver
which disciple betrayed jesus

entries.answer: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve apostles, betrayed Jesus (Matthew 10:4). He went to the chief priests and agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:14-16), and he came with the arresting crowd and identified Jesus with a kiss (Matthew 26:47-50).

entries.question: Who baptized Jesus?

entries.answer: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:13-17; Mark 1:9-11; Luke 3:21-22). John at first tried to prevent Him, saying, “I need to be baptized by You,” but Jesus replied that it was fitting to fulfil all righteousness (Matthew 3:14-15).

entries.question: Who wrote the book of Romans?

who is the author of romans
author of the book of romans
who wrote the letter to the romans
entries.answer: The apostle Paul wrote the letter to the Romans (Romans 1:1). A man named Tertius wrote it down for him and adds his own greeting (Romans 16:22).

who made the ark
who built the ark in the bible

entries.answer: Noah built the ark. God told him to make it of gopher wood (Genesis 6:14) and Noah did everything just as God commanded him (Genesis 6:22); the letter to the Hebrews adds that “by faith Noah… in godly fear built an ark to save his family” (Hebrews 11:7).

entries.question: Who killed Goliath?

who defeated goliath

entries.answer: David killed Goliath with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17:48-51): “David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him” (1 Samuel 17:50).
entries.note: 2 Samuel 21:19 and 1 Chronicles 20:5 tell of a later battle in which Elhanan killed a brother of Goliath (in the BSB's wording); some translations read 2 Samuel 21:19 as if Elhanan killed Goliath himself, and Christians explain the difference in more than one way.

entries.question: Who was swallowed by a great fish?

who was swallowed by the big fish
which prophet was swallowed by a fish

entries.answer: The prophet Jonah: “the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish” (Jonah 1:17). Jesus refers to this as a sign (Matthew 12:39-40).

entries.question: Who was the mother of Jesus?

who is the mother of jesus
who was jesus mother
who was the virgin mary
who gave birth to jesus
entries.answer: Mary was the mother of Jesus. She was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18; Luke 1:26-35). She was a relative of Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:36).

birthplace of jesus
which city was jesus born in
entries.answer: In Bethlehem in Judea (Matthew 2:1; Luke 2:4-7), as the prophet Micah had foretold: “you, Bethlehem Ephrathah… out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel” (Micah 5:2). Mary and Joseph had travelled there from Nazareth for the census (Luke 2:1-5).

entries.answer: Adam: God formed him from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Paul calls him “the first man Adam” (1 Corinthians 15:45).

entries.answer: Cain killed his brother Abel in the field (Genesis 4:8).

which is the shortest verse
entries.answer: “Jesus wept” (John 11:35) is the shortest verse in most English Bibles.

entries.answer: Daniel: at the king's command he was thrown into the den of lions (Daniel 6:16), and God kept him safe through the night (Daniel 6:22).

entries.answer: Stephen, one of the seven chosen to serve in Jerusalem, was stoned to death for his testimony about Jesus; as he died he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit… Lord, do not hold this sin against them” (Acts 7:54-60).

entries.note: The Bible does not call Stephen “the first martyr”; that is how the church has remembered him.

entries.answer: Joseph, the husband of Mary, was regarded as Jesus' father: Luke says Jesus “was regarded as the son of Joseph” (Luke 3:23). The Gospels teach that Jesus was conceived through the Holy Spirit, not by Joseph (Matthew 1:18-25).

how many commandments are in the bible

entries.answer: Ten: the Bible calls them “the Ten Commandments” (Exodus 34:28), written on two tablets of stone (Deuteronomy 4:13). They are given in Exodus 20:1-17 and repeated in Deuteronomy 5:6-21.

entries.question: Who were the twelve apostles?

how many disciples did jesus have
entries.answer: The twelve apostles were: Simon (called Peter) and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee and his brother John; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus (Matthew 10:2-4; the lists in Mark 3:16-19, Luke 6:14-16 and Acts 1:13 differ slightly in the names). Matthias was chosen to take the place of Judas (Acts 1:26).

entries.question: Who wrote the book of Revelation?

author of the book of revelation

entries.answer: The book names its writer as John: it was sent “to His servant John” (Revelation 1:1), and John writes “to the seven churches in the province of Asia” (Revelation 1:4); “I, John, your brother and partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance that are in Jesus, was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus” (Revelation 1:9).
entries.note: The book names John but does not say which John.

views.label: The traditional view
views.text: The writer is the apostle John, the son of Zebedee and the writer of the fourth Gospel, as many of the early church writers taught.

views.label: Another view
views.text: Some scholars think the writer was another man named John, such as a church leader in Asia, because the Greek and the style differ from the Gospel of John.

entries.question: Who was Paul before he became an apostle?

what was pauls name before

entries.answer: He was Saul, a young man who agreed with the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7:58), began to destroy the church by dragging believers off to prison (Acts 8:3), and was “still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord” (Acts 9:1) until the Lord met him on the road to Damascus. Luke then says, “Saul, who was also called Paul” (Acts 13:9), and he writes under the name Paul in his letters.

entries.answer: Jesus said the first and greatest commandment is, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind,” and the second is like it: “Love your neighbor as yourself.” All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments (Matthew 22:36-40; Mark 12:28-31).

entries.answer: The rule people call the golden rule is Jesus' teaching: “In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets” (Matthew 7:12; also Luke 6:31).
entries.note: The Bible does not use the name “golden rule”; it is the name given to this teaching later.

entries.question: What is the Sermon on the Mount?
alt_phrasings: the sermon on the mount
where is the sermon on the mount

what are the beatitudes
entries.answer: The Sermon on the Mount is Jesus' long teaching to His disciples and the crowds on a mountainside in Galilee, in Matthew 5 to 7: it opens with the Beatitudes (“Blessed are the poor in spirit…”, Matthew 5:3-12) and includes teaching on the Law, anger, adultery, oaths, loving enemies, giving, prayer and the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9-13), fasting, treasure, worry, judging others, asking and seeking, the narrow gate and the wise and foolish builders. “When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching, because He taught as one who had authority” (Matthew 7:28-29). Luke records a shorter teaching on level ground, often called the Sermon on the Plain (Luke 6:17-49).

citations.role: He went up on the mountain and taught

entries.question: Who was the strongest man in the Bible?

who had the greatest strength in the bible

entries.answer: Samson, the judge of Israel, is the Bible's strongest man: when “the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him” he tore a lion apart with his bare hands (Judges 14:6), struck down a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey (Judges 15:15) and carried off the doors and posts of a city gate on his shoulders (Judges 16:3). His strength was tied to his vow: a Nazirite from birth, he said, “If I am shaved, my strength will leave me” (Judges 16:17).
entries.note: The Bible does not name anyone “the strongest man”; Samson is the one the Bible shows doing the greatest feats of strength.

entries.question: Who was the wisest man in the Bible?

who was the wisest man who ever lived

entries.answer: Solomon. God said, “I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been nor will ever be another like you” (1 Kings 3:12), and Solomon “was wiser than all men” (1 Kings 4:31); his wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East and of Egypt (1 Kings 4:30). Jesus speaks of “One greater than Solomon” (Luke 11:31).

entries.question: Who was the tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus?

who climbed the sycamore tree to see jesus

entries.answer: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector in Jericho and a very wealthy man. He was small in stature and could not see over the crowd, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus (Luke 19:1-4). Jesus told him to come down because He must stay at his house, and said, “Today salvation has come to this house… the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost” (Luke 19:5-10).

entries.answer: Eve. God made a woman from the rib He had taken from the man and brought her to him (Genesis 2:22); “Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living” (Genesis 3:20).

who were the first two disciples
who did jesus call first
entries.answer: Matthew and Mark say Jesus first called two fishermen brothers by the Sea of Galilee, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew (“Come, follow Me… and I will make you fishers of men”), and then two other brothers, James and John, the sons of Zebedee (Matthew 4:18-22; Mark 1:16-20). John's Gospel tells how Andrew and another disciple of John the Baptist followed Jesus first, and Andrew then brought his brother Simon to Him (John 1:35-42).

Andrew and another follow Jesus first

entries.note: The Gospels tell the calling in more than one way; putting them together is the usual way of reading them.

entries.question: Who walked on water?

entries.answer: Jesus walked on the sea of Galilee toward His disciples in the fourth watch of the night (Matthew 14:25; Mark 6:48-49; John 6:19). Peter also walked on the water for a few steps when Jesus said “Come”, but began to sink when he saw the wind, and Jesus took hold of him (Matthew 14:28-31).

entries.question: How did Judas die?
alt_phrasings: how did judas iscariot die
what happened to judas
how did the betrayer of jesus die
did judas hang himself
what happened to judas after he betrayed jesus
entries.answer: Judas betrayed Jesus for money. He went to the chief priests and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” and they set out thirty pieces of silver for him (Matthew 26:14-16). When he saw that Jesus was condemned, “he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver” and said, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood” (Matthew 27:3-4). “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.” Judas “threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself” (Matthew 27:5): his guilt overwhelmed him and ended in his death. The priests would not put the money into the treasury, since it was “blood money”, and used it to buy the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners, which is why it is called the Field of Blood (Matthew 27:6-8). Acts 1:18-19 also speaks of the field bought with the payment for his wickedness; the two accounts differ in their details.

citations.role: his remorse, the silver and his death

entries.note: Matthew tells of his guilt and where it ended; the Bible does not give his thoughts, and does not say that he turned to the Lord for forgiveness.

entries.question: Where did Jesus die?

entries.question: How many people did Jesus feed with five loaves and two fish?

Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven and spoke a blessing, and the disciples gave the food to the people; all ate and were satisfied, and twelve basketfuls of pieces were left over (Matthew 14:15-21).

entries.question: What was the first miracle of Jesus?

entries.question: Where was Moses buried?

where was moses grave

entries.answer: Moses died in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said, and the LORD buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor; “no one to this day knows the location of his grave” (Deuteronomy 34:5-6). He died on Mount Nebo after seeing the promised land (Deuteronomy 34:1-4).

entries.question: What happened at Pentecost?
alt_phrasings: what happened on the day of pentecost
what is pentecost in the bible
the day of pentecost
when did the holy spirit come
what happened in acts 2
when was the holy spirit poured out
entries.answer: On the day of Pentecost the disciples were all together in one place when a sound like a mighty rushing wind filled the house, tongues like flames of fire came to rest on each of them, and “they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them” (Acts 2:1-4). A crowd gathered in bewilderment, because each one heard them speaking in his own language (Acts 2:6). Peter then preached, and about three thousand were baptized and added to the believers that day (Acts 2:14-41).

views.label: The Pentecostal reading
views.text: Pentecost is the pattern for the baptism in the Holy Spirit as an experience of its own after new birth, with speaking in tongues as the sign: “they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them” (Acts 2:4). The same happened in the house of Cornelius, “for they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God” (Acts 10:44-46), and to the disciples at Ephesus, “the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied” (Acts 19:6). It gives power for witness: “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses” (Acts 1:8). And it is for believers today: “This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off — to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself” (Acts 2:38-39).

views.label: Other views
views.text: Many traditions hold that Pentecost was a unique event, the church's birthday, and that every believer receives the Spirit at conversion; they understand the tongues of Acts 2 as known human languages and do not take the experience as a separate step.

entries.answer: The Gospels record seven sayings of Jesus from the cross: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing” (Luke 23:34); to the criminal beside Him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43); to His mother and the disciple He loved, “Woman, here is your son… Here is your mother” (John 19:26-27); “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34); “I am thirsty” (John 19:28); “It is finished” (John 19:30); and “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit” (Luke 23:46).
entries.note: Counting them as seven, and putting them in this order, is the church's way of gathering what the four Gospels record.

entries.question: What is the unforgivable sin?
alt_phrasings: what is the unpardonable sin

entries.answer: Jesus says that every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, “but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven… whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come” (Matthew 12:31-32). Mark adds that whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit “is guilty of eternal sin”, and explains why Jesus spoke: “because they were saying, ‘He has an unclean spirit’” (Mark 3:28-30; also Luke 12:10).
entries.note: The Bible does not define the sin beyond the setting in which Jesus spoke it.

views.label: What it means, in simple terms
views.text: It is knowingly and stubbornly saying that the work of the Holy Spirit is the work of the devil. Jesus drove out demons by the Spirit's power, and the scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,” and “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons” (Mark 3:22). Jesus answered that this kind of blasphemy against the Spirit “will not be forgiven” (Matthew 12:31-32). It is not a sin of weakness, a moment of doubt or a word said in anger: it is a hardened refusal to see God at work, to the end. The promise to everyone who comes to Christ still stands: “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9), and “the one who comes to Me I will never drive away” (John 6:37). For that reason many pastors, ministers and priests say that a person who is troubled about having committed this sin, and wants to be forgiven, is not showing the hardened heart that Jesus described.

views.label: Another reading
views.text: It is the settled refusal of the Spirit's witness to Christ all the way to death, which leaves nothing by which a person can be forgiven; it is not a single word spoken in anger.

entries.question: What does the Bible say about money?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about wealth
what does the bible say about riches
is money the root of all evil
does the bible say money is evil

entries.answer: The Bible does not say that money is evil; it says that “the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil” (1 Timothy 6:10). Jesus says, “You cannot serve both God and money” (Matthew 6:24) and warns, “Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions” (Luke 12:15). Believers are told to “be content with what you have” (Hebrews 13:5), and the rich “not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God”, and to be “generous and ready to share” (1 Timothy 6:17-19). “He who loves money is never satisfied by money” (Ecclesiastes 5:10).
entries.note: This gathers what the Bible says about money in many places; it is not one passage.

views.label: The tithe and the firstfruits
views.text: God asked His people for the first and the best: “any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD” (Leviticus 27:30); “Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest; then your barns will be filled with plenty” (Proverbs 3:9-10); “Bring the full tithe into the storehouse… Test Me in this” (Malachi 3:10). Jesus did not set the tithe aside: “You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former” (Matthew 23:23). Many hold that this principle still applies.

views.label: Giving from the heart, in the New Testament
views.text: “Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver” (2 Corinthians 9:7), and “whoever sows generously will also reap generously” (2 Corinthians 9:6). Jesus watched the crowd putting money into the treasury and said of the poor widow who put in two small copper coins, “this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury… she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on” (Mark 12:41-44; Luke 21:1-4). What counts is not the amount but the surrender and the trust that God will provide: “my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus” (Philippians 4:19).

views.label: Both together
views.text: Many hold that the two belong together: the tithe and the firstfruits teach that the first and the best belongs to God, and the New Testament shows the spirit in which to give, freely, in surrender and trust in God, and not by a rule about the amount.

entries.answer: Matthias. After Peter said that one of the men who had accompanied them from John's baptism until Jesus was taken up must become a witness of the resurrection with them (Acts 1:21-22), they proposed two men, Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias (Acts 1:23). views.label: One answer: Matthias
views.text: The eleven prayed, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen,” they cast lots, and “the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles” (Acts 1:24-26). Many hold that Matthias was rightly chosen, under God's guidance, to fill Judas's place among the Twelve.

views.label: Another answer: Paul
views.text: Some hold that the eleven chose by lot before the Spirit had come, and that God's own twelfth apostle was Paul, who calls himself “an apostle — sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father” (Galatians 1:1) and “the least of the apostles” (1 Corinthians 15:9). Matthias is not named again in the New Testament.

entries.question: What does it mean to fear the Lord?
alt_phrasings: what is the fear of the lord

entries.answer: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” (Proverbs 1:7) and “the beginning of wisdom” (Proverbs 9:10; Psalms 111:10). “To fear the LORD is to hate evil” (Proverbs 8:13). The Preacher concludes, “Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man” (Ecclesiastes 12:13).

citations.role: fear God and keep His commandments

views.label: Reverence is the key
views.text: Reverence and awe are the heart of the fear of the LORD: “let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe” (Hebrews 12:28). The believer honours God's awesome power, might, love and grace, and turns from evil because of who He is (Proverbs 8:13; Exodus 20:20).

views.label: The fear of God's judgement and power
views.text: Scripture also speaks of fearing God's power and judgement: “Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell” (Luke 12:5), and “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God” (Hebrews 10:31). Many hold that this fear belongs to those who reject Christ, and that believers, who know their salvation and God's grace, do not live in dread: “there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:1); “you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of sonship” (Romans 8:15); “perfect love drives out fear” (1 John 4:18). They stand in awe of God's power and love Him with reverence, not with fear. Others note that Jesus spoke Luke 12:4-5 to “My friends” and that Hebrews 10:30 says “The Lord will judge His people”, so for them a sober respect for God's judgement remains part of reverence.

entries.answer: Jesus told this parable in Luke 15:11-32. A man had two sons. The younger asked for his share of the estate, journeyed to a distant country and “squandered his wealth in wild living” (Luke 15:13). When a famine came he ended up feeding pigs, and “finally he came to his senses” (Luke 15:17) and decided to go home and say, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you” (Luke 15:18). “While he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him” (Luke 15:20), and called for the best robe, a ring and a feast: “For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!” (Luke 15:24). The older son, who had stayed at home, became angry and refused to go in, and the father pleaded with him: “Son, you are always with me,” the father said, “and all that is mine is yours. But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found” (Luke 15:28-32). Jesus told it with the lost sheep and the lost coin, to answer those who grumbled that He welcomed sinners (Luke 15:1-2).

entries.answer: Jesus told this parable (Luke 10:25-37) when an expert in the law asked, “And who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29). A man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho fell into the hands of robbers, who left him “half dead” (Luke 10:30). A priest and then a Levite saw him and “passed by on the other side” (Luke 10:31-32), but a Samaritan “looked at him and had compassion”: he bandaged his wounds, put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and gave the innkeeper two denarii, promising to repay any extra expense (Luke 10:33-35). Jesus asked which of the three was a neighbor to the man; the expert answered, “The one who showed him mercy,” and Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise” (Luke 10:36-37).

entries.answer: Jesus said that “the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom”; five were foolish and five were wise, and the foolish took no extra oil (Matthew 25:1-4). When the bridegroom was delayed they all fell asleep, and at midnight the cry rang out, “Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!” (Matthew 25:5-6). The foolish asked the wise for oil and were told to go and buy some, and “while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut” (Matthew 25:10). The others came later and said, “Lord, lord, open the door for us!” but he replied, “Truly I tell you, I do not know you” (Matthew 25:11-12). Jesus ends, “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour” (Matthew 25:13).
entries.note: The parable does not say what the oil stands for.

views.label: The Pentecostal reading
views.text: Many Pentecostal and other believers read the parable as a call to be ready for the Lord's return, the coming of the bridegroom, and take the oil to be the Holy Spirit: those who are ready go in with Him (Matthew 25:10, 13).

views.label: Other readings
views.text: Others take the oil to mean real faith, or a life of obedience, or simply being ready; the parable itself does not say what the oil is.

Jesus says, “there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent” (Luke 15:7). Matthew tells it too (Matthew 18:12-14).

For example: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven”; “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God”; “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.” Luke 6:20-23 records a similar list.

entries.answer: Jesus told of a farmer who went out to sow his seed (Matthew 13:3). Some seed fell along the path and the birds devoured it, some fell on rocky ground and withered because it had no root, some fell among thorns that choked it, and some fell on good soil and “produced a crop — a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold” (Matthew 13:4-8). He explained it: the path is the one who hears the message but does not understand it, and the evil one snatches it away (Matthew 13:19); the rocky ground is the one who receives it with joy but falls away when trouble or persecution comes (Matthew 13:20-21); among the thorns “the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word” (Matthew 13:22); and the good soil “is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit” (Matthew 13:23). Mark and Luke tell it too (Mark 4:1-20; Luke 8:4-15).

Then the wall of the city will collapse” (Joshua 6:5). “So when the rams' horns sounded, the people shouted… and the wall collapsed. entries.question: What is Easter?

entries.answer: “Easter” is a modern reference. The Bible speaks of the Passover and of the resurrection of Jesus, which the app calls Resurrection Sunday. The Passover to the LORD “begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month” (Leviticus 23:5), and Paul writes that “Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed” (1 Corinthians 5:7). Jesus rose on the first day of the week: “After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week” the women went to the tomb (Matthew 28:1), and the angel said, “He is not here; He has risen, just as He said!” (Matthew 28:6; Luke 24:1-3; John 20:1). Paul gives it as of first importance that Christ died for our sins, “was buried” and “was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures” (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). The word “Easter” appears once in the King James Version, in Acts 12:4 (“intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people”), where the Greek word is pascha, “Passover”; the BSB, ASV, WEB and Young's Literal Translation all read “Passover” there.
entries.note: The app uses the Bible's terms (Passover and Resurrection Sunday); “Easter” is shown only as a modern reference.

entries.question: Who wrote the book of Hebrews?
alt_phrasings: who wrote hebrews
who is the author of hebrews

entries.answer: The letter to the Hebrews does not name its author. Unlike Paul's letters it opens with no greeting and no name. Its closing lines show that the writer belonged to Timothy's circle (Hebrews 13:23) and sent greetings from believers in Italy (Hebrews 13:24). Through the centuries the church has suggested Paul, Barnabas (a Levite, Acts 4:36), Apollos (a learned man who knew the Scriptures well, Acts 18:24) and Priscilla with Aquila. The early church was divided: the East came to receive it as Paul's, while the West for a time doubted that, and the scholar Origen is remembered for saying that only God truly knows who wrote it. Whoever the human writer was, the church has always received Hebrews as inspired Scripture.
entries.note: Hebrews is anonymous in the text itself; every name given to its author is a tradition or a guess.

entries.question: Why did Jesus weep at the tomb of Lazarus?

entries.answer: John 11:35 is the shortest verse in many Bibles: “Jesus wept.” When Jesus saw Mary and those with her weeping, “He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled” (John 11:33). He wept although He knew what He was about to do: He had told His disciples that He was going to wake Lazarus (John 11:11) and had promised Martha that her brother would rise again (John 11:23). So His tears were not doubt. They show His love for Lazarus and for the grieving family (the onlookers said, “See how He loved him!”, John 11:36) and His sorrow over what death does to those He made. Scripture then shows that sorrow turn to power when He cries “Lazarus, come out!” (John 11:43). Hebrews 4:15 says that we have a High Priest who sympathizes with our weaknesses.

entries.question: What does the Bible say to comfort us when someone dies?
alt_phrasings: verses for when someone dies

entries.answer: The Bible does not tell the grieving to hide their tears. Jesus Himself wept at the grave of a friend (John 11:35), and He blesses those who mourn: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted” (Matthew 5:4). “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit” (Psalm 34:18); even in the darkest valley the believer need not fear, for God is with him (Psalm 23:4). The God of all comfort comforts us so that we can comfort others (2 Corinthians 1:3-4). For those who belong to Christ there is hope: Jesus said, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies” (John 11:25). Paul writes so that we do not grieve “like the rest, who are without hope” (1 Thessalonians 4:13-18), because the dead in Christ will rise when the Lord returns, and we will be with Him forever. Jesus has gone to prepare a place and will come back for His own (John 14:1-3). At the end God “will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain” (Revelation 21:4).
entries.note: The Browse area has a page of verses for grief and loss.

entries.question: What happens to a believer when they die?
alt_phrasings: what happens after we die
what happens when you die
what happens when a christian dies

what does the bible say about life after death
is there life after death
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus told the thief on the cross, “today you will be with Me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43). Paul said that to die is gain and that he desired “to depart and be with Christ, which is far better” (Philippians 1:21-23), and that to be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord (2 Corinthians 5:8). Human beings die once, and after that comes judgment (Hebrews 9:27). The believer's body waits for the resurrection: at Christ's return “the dead in Christ will be the first to rise” (1 Thessalonians 4:16), and the perishable is raised imperishable (1 Corinthians 15:51-54). The unbelieving dead face the judgment before the great white throne (Revelation 20:11-15).

Pentecostal understanding: the believer is at once in the conscious presence of the Lord, then is raised with a glorified body at the Rapture and the resurrection of the just; the unbeliever awaits final judgment (Luke 16:22-26; Revelation 20:11-15).

Other views: some (Seventh-day Adventists, Jehovah's Witnesses) hold that the dead are unconscious, in “sleep”, until the resurrection; Roman Catholic teaching adds purgatory for those who still need cleansing before heaven; some Christians believe the lost are finally destroyed instead of suffering without end.

entries.question: Why did God harden Pharaoh's heart?
alt_phrasings: why did god harden pharaohs heart
did god harden pharaoh's heart

entries.answer:
Scripture: before the plagues God told Moses, “I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go” (Exodus 4:21). The record then says both things. Pharaoh hardened his own heart: when he saw that there was relief, he hardened it (Exodus 8:15), and he did so again after the plague of hail (Exodus 9:34-35). Later “the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart” (Exodus 9:12; 10:1, 20, 27). God's purpose was to show His power and make His name known in all the earth (Exodus 9:16), and Paul quotes that in Romans 9:17-18, “God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.”

Pentecostal understanding: God hardened a heart that had already refused Him again and again, confirming the choice Pharaoh had made (Exodus 8:15, 32; 9:34); it is judgment on persistent unbelief, not a denial of free will.

Other views: Reformed teachers read Romans 9 as God's sovereign choice, in which He hardens some and shows mercy to others; many scholars note that the Hebrew is used of both Pharaoh and God, and that God's hardening came after Pharaoh's own.

entries.question: What was Paul's thorn in the flesh?
alt_phrasings: what did paul mean by thorn in the flesh

entries.answer:
Scripture: after being caught up to the third heaven, Paul says, “there was given me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me” so that he would not become conceited (2 Corinthians 12:7). He pleaded with the Lord three times that it would leave him, and the Lord answered, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness” (2 Corinthians 12:8-9). Paul therefore delights in weakness, for “when I am weak, then I am strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). The Bible does not say what the thorn was.

Pentecostal understanding: many read it as a satanic affliction or opposition allowed by God to keep Paul humble, not as proof that God no longer heals; the same Paul saw many healed (Acts 19:11-12; Acts 28:8-9). In Scripture “thorns in your sides” is a picture of enemies and opponents (Numbers 33:55; Judges 2:3).

Other views: a bodily illness (such as eye trouble, suggested by Galatians 4:13-15 and 6:11), or a temptation, or a persecutor of Paul's ministry; the church has never settled it.

entries.question: Is cremation allowed for Christians?
alt_phrasings: is cremation allowed in the bible
is cremation a sin
does the bible forbid cremation
burial or cremation bible
can christians be cremated
what does the bible say about cremation
entries.answer:
Scripture: the Bible gives no command about cremation. Burial is the usual practice in both Testaments (Genesis 23:19; Genesis 50:13; John 19:40-42; Acts 8:2), and the body returns to dust as God said in Genesis 3:19. Fire for the dead is mentioned without comment in 1 Samuel 31:12-13, where the men of Jabesh Gilead burned the bodies of Saul and his sons and then buried their bones, and David blessed them for their kindness (2 Samuel 2:4-6). Burning the bones of a king in contempt is condemned (Amos 2:1). The resurrection does not depend on the condition of the body: the sea and death give up their dead (Revelation 20:13), and the body is raised by God's power (1 Corinthians 15:35-44).

Pentecostal understanding: many Pentecostal and evangelical churches prefer burial because it follows the Bible's pattern and pictures the hope of resurrection, yet most leave cremation to the conscience of the family before God, since Scripture does not forbid it.

Other views: the Catholic Church allows cremation if it is not chosen to deny the resurrection; the Orthodox churches generally require burial; Jewish and Muslim tradition forbids cremation.

entries.question: What does the Bible say about anger?

entries.answer: Anger itself is not always sin, but it must be controlled: “Be angry, yet do not sin.” “Do not let the sun set upon your anger” (Ephesians 4:26-27). “Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, for man's anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires” (James 1:19-20). “A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger” (Proverbs 15:1). A fool gives full vent to his anger, but a wise man holds it back (Proverbs 29:11), and one who is slow to anger has great understanding (Proverbs 14:29). “Refrain from anger and abandon wrath” (Psalm 37:8). Believers are told to put away anger, wrath, malice and filthy talk (Colossians 3:8). Jesus warned that anger toward a brother puts us in danger of judgment (Matthew 5:22) and Paul says not to take revenge, but leave room for God's wrath (Romans 12:19). God Himself is “compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion” (Psalm 103:8).

entries.question: What does agape mean?

entries.answer: Agape is the Greek word the New Testament uses for self-giving love, a love that seeks the good of the other whatever it costs. It is the love of God: “God is love” (1 John 4:8). It was shown at the cross (John 3:16; Romans 5:8), Jesus commands His followers to love one another in the same way (John 13:34-35), and Paul describes it in 1 Corinthians 13:4-7 and calls love the greatest of faith, hope and love (1 Corinthians 13:13). The Greek has other words for love, such as phileo, the love of friendship and affection. Jesus and Peter use both words in John 21:15-17. The New Testament never uses eros, the word for romantic desire.

entries.answer: Scripture says three days. Jesus said that the Son of Man would be “three days and three nights” in the heart of the earth, as Jonah was in the great fish (Matthew 12:40), and the apostles preach that He was raised “on the third day” (1 Corinthians 15:4; Luke 24:46). He was buried on the day of Preparation, just before the Sabbath began (Luke 23:50-56; John 19:42), and the tomb was found empty at dawn on the first day of the week (Luke 24:1-3; John 20:1). In Jewish reckoning any part of a day counts as a day, so Friday afternoon, the Sabbath and Sunday morning are “three days”. Some teachers hold to a Wednesday or Thursday crucifixion to make three full nights; most place it on Friday.

entries.answer: Marriage begins with God: a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and “they will become one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Jesus affirms it: “what God has joined together, let man not separate” (Matthew 19:4-6). The husband is to love his wife as Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her, and the wife is to respect her husband (Ephesians 5:22-33); husbands are to treat their wives with understanding and honour (1 Peter 3:7). “Marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept undefiled” (Hebrews 13:4). Husband and wife owe each other faithfulness and affection (1 Corinthians 7:2-5), and marriage is a covenant before God (Malachi 2:14-16). Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing (Proverbs 18:22).

entries.answer:
Scripture: on the night He was betrayed Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me,” and the cup was “the new covenant in My blood” (Luke 22:19-20). Paul passes on the same words and adds that each time we eat the bread and drink the cup we proclaim the Lord's death until He comes (1 Corinthians 11:23-26). The cup and bread are a participation in the blood and body of Christ (1 Corinthians 10:16). Each person is to examine himself and not eat and drink in an unworthy manner (1 Corinthians 11:27-29).

Pentecostal understanding: Communion is an ordinance of remembrance, thanksgiving and fellowship, in which the bread and cup picture Christ's body and blood and the Lord is present by His Spirit among His people; it is taken with self-examination and often with prayer for healing (1 Corinthians 11:30).

Other views: Roman Catholic and Orthodox teaching holds that the bread and wine truly become Christ's body and blood (transubstantiation in the Catholic wording); Lutherans hold His real presence “in, with and under” the bread and wine; Reformed churches teach a real spiritual presence; many Baptist and Evangelical churches hold it to be a memorial.

entries.answer: “Pastor” means shepherd. Christ gave His church “apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers” to equip the saints for the work of ministry (Ephesians 4:11-12). Pastors are told to shepherd God's flock willingly, not for gain and not lording it over them, and to be examples, and the Chief Shepherd will reward them (1 Peter 5:1-4); they are to guard the flock over which the Holy Spirit has made them overseers (Acts 20:28). The words elder, overseer and shepherd describe the same office (Acts 20:17, 28; Titus 1:5-7). Qualifications are listed in 1 Timothy 3:1-7 and Titus 1:5-9: blameless, faithful to his wife, self-controlled, able to teach, and not a lover of money. Elders who direct the affairs of the church well are worthy of double honour, especially those who labour at preaching and teaching (1 Timothy 5:17), and the people are to respond to their leaders, who watch over their souls (Hebrews 13:17). God promised “shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding” (Jeremiah 3:15).

entries.question: What is the meaning of life according to the Bible?

entries.answer: Scripture gives the purpose of life in several places. We were created for God's glory (Isaiah 43:7), and whatever we do, we are to do it for the glory of God (1 Corinthians 10:31). “Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man” (Ecclesiastes 12:13). The two greatest commandments sum it up: to love the Lord with all the heart, soul and mind, and to love our neighbour as ourselves (Matthew 22:37-40). Eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent (John 17:3). All things were created through Christ and for Him (Colossians 1:16), and from Him, through Him and to Him are all things (Romans 11:36). Jesus came so that we might have life and have it abundantly (John 10:10). We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works (Ephesians 2:10).

entries.answer: Jesus said, “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,” so that we may be sons of our Father in heaven (Matthew 5:43-48; Luke 6:27-36). Paul says: bless those who persecute you; do not repay evil for evil; if your enemy is hungry, feed him; and “overcome evil with good” (Romans 12:14-21). Proverbs gives the same word: if your enemy is hungry, give him food (Proverbs 25:21-22), and do not gloat when he falls (Proverbs 24:17). The Law already commanded kindness to an enemy's ox or donkey that had strayed (Exodus 23:4-5). Jesus on the cross prayed, “Father, forgive them” (Luke 23:34), and Stephen did the same as he was stoned (Acts 7:60).

entries.answer: God commands care for the poor. Israel was told to open its hand to the needy brother (Deuteronomy 15:7-11) and to leave the edges of the field and the gleanings for the poor and the foreigner (Leviticus 19:9-10). “Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him” (Proverbs 14:31), and “Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender” (Proverbs 19:17). Jesus began His ministry to bring good news to the poor (Luke 4:18) and said that what we do for the least of His brothers we do for Him (Matthew 25:34-40). James warns against favouring the rich over the poor (James 2:1-9) and John asks how God's love can be in anyone who sees a brother in need and shuts up his heart (1 John 3:17). Paul was eager to remember the poor (Galatians 2:10).

entries.answer: “Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see” (Hebrews 11:1). Without faith it is impossible to please God, because whoever comes to Him must believe that He exists and rewards those who seek Him (Hebrews 11:6). Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ (Romans 10:17). We are saved by grace through faith, and this is the gift of God (Ephesians 2:8-9). “The righteous will live by faith” (Romans 1:17; Habakkuk 2:4), we walk by faith and not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7), and faith without works is dead (James 2:17). Jesus tells us to have faith in God (Mark 11:22-24).

entries.answer: Grace (Greek charis) is God's favour, freely given and not earned. “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith” (Ephesians 2:8-9), and it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast. We are “justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus” (Romans 3:24). The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people, and it teaches us to say no to ungodliness (Titus 2:11-12). From Christ's fullness we have all received “grace upon grace” (John 1:16-17). His grace is sufficient for us, and His power is perfected in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9). Where sin increased, grace increased all the more (Romans 5:20), yet grace is never a licence to sin (Romans 6:1-2, 14).

entries.question: What is heaven like?

entries.answer: The Bible describes heaven in pictures, because it is beyond our experience: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him” (1 Corinthians 2:9). Jesus speaks of His Father's house with many rooms, which He is going to prepare (John 14:2-3). In Revelation God makes His dwelling with His people, wipes away every tear, and there is no more death, mourning, crying or pain (Revelation 21:3-4). The New Jerusalem has no need of sun or moon, because the glory of God gives it light (Revelation 21:23); the river of the water of life flows from the throne and the tree of life grows beside it (Revelation 22:1-2), and God's servants will see His face (Revelation 22:3-5). In His presence is fullness of joy (Psalm 16:11). The redeemed will worship and serve Him (Revelation 7:9-17).

entries.question: What is the Day of the Lord?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible mean by the day of the lord

entries.answer:
Scripture: the prophets speak of a day when God steps in openly to judge the proud and rescue His people: “the day of the LORD is near” (Joel 1:15; 2:1-2, 31; Isaiah 13:6-9; Zephaniah 1:14-18). It is darkness and not light for the wicked (Amos 5:18-20), and it ends with the LORD as king over all the earth (Zechariah 14:1-9). In the New Testament it “will come like a thief in the night” (1 Thessalonians 5:2-4; 2 Peter 3:10), and Paul says that day will not come until the rebellion occurs and the man of lawlessness is revealed (2 Thessalonians 2:1-3). Believers are not appointed to wrath but to obtain salvation (1 Thessalonians 5:9).

Pentecostal understanding: the Day of the Lord begins after the Rapture with the Tribulation judgments, and includes the return of Christ in glory and the final judgment, ending with the new heavens and new earth (2 Peter 3:10-13).

Other views: some read the prophets' “day” as past judgments such as Babylon's fall and Jerusalem's destruction (and as foreshadowing the end); those who hold one single return of Christ say that the Day of the Lord is that one day of His coming and the judgment.
